kept.title: The per-instantiation P scratch isolation that the comment and the PR body rely on has no effect on the 4-head results.
kept.body: Check: 'Is the kv_mul-4 path unchanged?' (PR body, How to review, item 3) cites 'The thread_local P scratch is one per instantiation' as a reason. The comment at HEAD says: 'A function template's static locals exist once per specialization. This scratch therefore belongs to the 4-head or the 16-head instantiation only, and a 4-head call never sees a 16-head call's rows.' [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:279-283]. The fact is true, but the conclusion it protects has no consequence. In TDPBF16PS, output row i comes only from row i of the A operand (P), which Note [Tile stores write 16 rows] itself states: 'output row i of a tile multiply comes from row i of the A operand' [h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:104-105]. So even a scratch shared by both instantiations would change only rows 4..15 of `o` after a 16-head call, and the 4-head caller ignores those rows ('callers read rows 0..group_heads-1 and ignore the rest' [amx_attn_iface.hpp:105]; self_attention.hpp copies only `offset < operation_kv_mul` rows out of amx_o [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1795-1800]). Reading cost: a reviewer following the PR body looks for a hazard that does not exist, and the sentence 'so the padded tile rows contribute nothing' reads as if nonzero padding rows could corrupt the real rows. Proposed fix (comment only): replace the last three sentences with 'A function template's static locals exist once per specialization, so the 4-head instantiation's rows 4..15 stay zero after a 16-head call on the same thread. That keeps rows 4..15 of `o` zero; the caller ignores those rows either way.' and drop the 'thread_local P scratch' bullet from the PR body's item 3, or restate it the same way.
kept.rule: PR review: build and link consistency / claim matches code (PR body item 'Is the kv_mul-4 path unchanged?')
kept.evidence:
279:  //   the padded tile rows contribute nothing. A function template's static
280:  //   locals exist once per specialization. This scratch therefore belongs to
281:  //   the 4-head or the 16-head instantiation only, and a 4-head call never
282:  //   sees a 16-head call's rows. For 16 heads every row is written, so there
283:  //   is no padding.
corrections: The iface citation should read h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:103-105 (the sentence starts at line 103 with "corrupted. Rows group_heads..15 of `o` are the products of the kernel's"), not 104-105.

Two small adjustments to the proposed fix. (1) The body objects to "so the padded tile rows contribute nothing" (amx_attn.cpp:278-279) as suggesting cross-row corruption, but the proposed replacement keeps that phrase; replace it too, for example "rows group_heads..15 are zero padding (never written after thread init), so rows group_heads..15 of `o` come out zero". (2) Do not let the comment imply the `= {}` zero-init is pointless: it still keeps the tile load from reading uninitialized memory, so the suggested wording should keep "zero padding" and only drop the per-instantiation isolation sentences. Suggested full replacement for lines 276-283: "// P: 16 rows x 64 bf16 bit patterns (the AVX-512 convert instruction writes raw 16-bit lanes, so this scratch stays uint16_t). Rows group_heads..15 are zero padding (never written after thread init); they produce rows group_heads..15 of `o`, which every caller ignores (Note [Tile stores write 16 rows]). Each instantiation has its own copy of this static, so the 4-head copy's padding rows stay zero even after a 16-head call on the same thread." In the PR body, the "thread_local P scratch is one per instantiation" bullet under "Is the kv_mul-4 path unchanged?" can be dropped or restated as "the per-instantiation P scratch only affects rows of `o` that callers ignore".
refutations:
Refuted on the rule lens and partly on scope.

Rule ("claim matches code"): every claim in the comment matches the code, and the finder concedes this ("The fact is true"). The comment says the scratch belongs to one instantiation and "a 4-head call never sees a 16-head call's rows" [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:280-282]; it does not claim that the real rows 0..3 would be corrupted otherwise. A true claim that matches the code is not a finding under this rule. The complaint is about comment necessity and wording, which is a simplify-cpp-comments concern, not the PR-review rule the finding names.

The finding's central point ("has no consequence") is also wrong with respect to the documented contract. The same comment states that rows group_heads..15 of P are "never written after thread init" [amx_attn.cpp:277-278]. In a function template that claim is only true if the scratch is per instantiation: with a shared scratch, a 16-head call would write rows 4..15 and the 4-head instantiation would then read them. The public Note [Tile stores write 16 rows] relies on it too: "Rows group_heads..15 of `o` are the products of the kernel's zero padding rows of P" [h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:103-105]. The per-instantiation sentences are what keeps both statements true at HEAD, so they are load-bearing for the comments, not decorative. The PR body item asks whether the kv_mul-4 *path* is unchanged [pr-body.md:39-41]; per-instantiation storage is what makes the 4-head instantiation write the same 16 rows of `o` as the BASE function did (rows 4..15 zero), so it is a correct reason to list there, even though self_attention.hpp copies only rows 0..kv_mul-1 [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1795-1800] and t_amx_numerics checks only rows 0..group_heads-1 [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:274].

Scope: the wording the finder objects to, "so the padded tile rows contribute nothing", is BASE text unchanged by the diff (BASE amx_attn.cpp:229-231: "rows 4..15 are zero padding (never written after thread init), so the padded tile rows contribute nothing"). Only the three sentences about per-specialization static locals are new (diff lines 143-146), and those are the true, load-bearing ones.

kept.title: The PR body says a caller with an unlisted group size "fails to link"; at HEAD it fails to compile at the requires-clause, before any link step.
kept.body: PR-body check (section "How to review this PR", question 2, second bullet): "the explicit instantiations at the end of the file: the same two sizes. A caller with any other size fails to link." The code does not support "fails to link". Every kernel declaration carries a constraint [h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:202-204]: `template <size_t group_heads>` / `  requires(group_heads_ok(group_heads))` / `void pack_q_group_128x4(...)`. A call such as `pack_q_group_128x4<8>(...)` therefore has no viable candidate and the compiler rejects it (constraints not satisfied). The linker is never reached. A link failure can happen only for a size that passes group_heads_ok but has no explicit instantiation in amx_attn.cpp:333-354, and the comment at amx_attn.cpp:330-332 states that the two lists are equal, so that case does not exist at HEAD either. Reading cost: a reviewer who tests the claim by adding `<8>` sees a compile error and then doubts the rest of the bullet. Proposed replacement for the sentence: "A caller with any other size fails to compile: the requires-clause on every declaration rejects it. The instantiation list and group_heads_ok must stay equal, or a size that passes the gate would fail to link instead."
kept.rule: PR-body claims checked against the code at HEAD (reviewer lens: every sentence in "How to review this PR")

h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:204: void pack_q_group_128x4(const bf16* q_group, bf16* packed) noexcept;

kept.title: The PR body names the stage-3/stage-4 shuffle "vshufps"; the code uses _mm512_shuffle_f32x4, which is VSHUFF32X4, a different instruction with a different selector meaning.
kept.body: PR-body check (section "How to review this PR", question 1, first bullet): "row `4*l + k` of `s` uses the `vshufps` selector `0x88` when bit 0 of `l` is 0 and `0xdd` when it is 1." The code at HEAD [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:178-181] calls `_mm512_shuffle_f32x4(u[0][k], u[1][k], pair_sel)` and `_mm512_shuffle_f32x4(p, q2, quad_sel)`. That intrinsic compiles to VSHUFF32X4 (shuffle of 128-bit lanes). VSHUFPS (`_mm512_shuffle_ps`) shuffles 32-bit elements inside each 128-bit lane, and its 8-bit immediate selects elements, not lanes. With VSHUFPS the selector values 0x88 and 0xdd would not mean "even lanes" and "odd lanes", so a reviewer who looks up vshufps to check the selector reasoning reaches the wrong table. The object-compare row in [Verification] hedges with "40 `vshuf` shuffles", which is consistent with either name. Proposed fix in the PR body: replace "the `vshufps` selector" with "the `_mm512_shuffle_f32x4` (VSHUFF32X4, 128-bit lane shuffle) selector".
kept.rule: PR-body claims checked against the code at HEAD (function and instruction names)
corrections: Replace the sentence "With VSHUFPS the selector values 0x88 and 0xdd would not mean "even lanes" and "odd lanes", so a reviewer who looks up vshufps to check the selector reasoning reaches the wrong table." with: "Under VSHUFPS the same immediates 0x88 and 0xdd select even and odd 32-bit elements inside each 128-bit lane, not even and odd 128-bit lanes, so a reviewer who follows question 1 with the vshufps table cannot reproduce the "lane `l` becomes row `4*l + k`" argument, which needs whole 128-bit lanes to move." Also add: "The code comment at [amx_attn.cpp:154-157] already names `_mm512_shuffle_f32x4`; only the PR body needs the change."

kept.title: The Verification table says the kill-switch run skipped "2 sections"; the skip happens at the test-case level, so 2 test cases (4 sections) are skipped.
kept.body: PR-body check (section "Verification", table "Builds and tests", row "AMX off (kill switch)"): "2 sections skipped with 'AMX unavailable on this host'". At HEAD the availability check sits before any SECTION [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:316-319 and 330-333]: `if (!tron::amx_attn_h128g4::available()) { WARN("AMX unavailable on this host - QK precision check skipped"); return; }`. The return leaves the test case before Catch2 enters either of its two sections ("4 heads: ..." at line 320 and "16 heads: ..." at line 323, and "4 heads" / "16 heads" at lines 334 and 337). So the run skips 2 test cases, which hold 4 sections. Reading cost: a reader who counts sections in the file (two per case) cannot match the number 2. Proposed replacement: "2 test cases (the QK and PV precision checks, 4 sections) skipped with 'AMX unavailable on this host'".
kept.rule: PR-body claims checked against the code at HEAD (numbers the code fixes)
corrections: Optional shortening of the proposed replacement: "2 test cases (the QK and PV precision checks) skipped with 'AMX unavailable on this host'". The "4 sections" count is correct but not needed; keep "4 pass" unchanged, because Catch2 WARN leaves both skipped cases in the passed count.

kept.title: The query-fill comment credits the per-head offset with catching "a pack that permutes or drops heads", but the pack in this test is a fake that copies in order; the break the offset detects is a wrong q pointer from the dispatch.
kept.body: Test check (what deliberate code break makes the new assertion fail). The comment [t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:142-143] says: "Each head carries its own offset (i / head_size), so a pack that permutes or drops heads cannot pass". In this translation unit the pack is the fake at lines 257-264, which copies `input[0 .. group_heads * HEAD_SIZE_128)` into `probe.q` in order; no real packer runs, so a permuting pack is not a break this file can see. A dropping pack is caught without the offset: a missing head leaves `probe.q[i]` at 0, and every `expected[i]` is at least 1.0. What the offset does add is a check on the pointer the dispatch passes [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1697: `q.data + kv_head * geometry.kv_mul() * geometry.kv.head_size`]: with the old fill `1.0f + (i % 4) * 0.25f`, a pointer offset by a whole head reads values identical to the expected ones, so the assertion at line 237 could not fail; with the per-head offset it fails. The assertion is not vacuous, but the comment names the wrong component. Proposed replacement for the two sentences: "Each head carries its own offset (i / head_size), so a q pointer that starts at the wrong head cannot pass (the fake pack copies the pointed-at values in order). Every value is exact in bf16."
kept.rule: Tests lens: does the section/comment name what the assertion asserts; what code break makes the assertion fail
corrections: Two sentences in the body overstate what the offset guards. (1) In this test n_kv_heads = 1 [t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:82], so kv_head is 0 and the term `kv_head * geometry.kv_mul() * geometry.kv.head_size` at self_attention.hpp:1697 is always 0; a wrong multiplier in that expression is invisible here. Say instead that the offset checks that the pointer handed to the packer starts at head 0 of the job's q (for example, a wrong job index or an added offset), not that it checks the kv_head arithmetic at 1697. (2) "with the old fill ... the assertion at line 237 could not fail" is not certain: a pointer offset by +128 makes the last head read past the job's group into the next job's qs_roped, whose content the test does not set; if that memory is zero the old fill already fails on the last head. Soften to "with the old fill (period 4), the first n_heads-1 heads read values identical to the expected ones". The proposed replacement comment text is fine as written.

Add to the comment text: in this test n_kv_heads = 1 [t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:81], so the dispatch's `kv_head * kv_mul * head_size` term is always 0; the wrong-pointer break the offset guards is a dispatch that derives the start from something other than kv_head. Optionally mention that the round-2 fill at lines 180-183 has no per-head offset, so the property holds only for the first round.

Minor precision for the posted text: in this fixture n_kv_heads = 1 (line 82) so kv_head is 0 and the start address is q.data whatever the kv_mul multiplier; the offset therefore guards a start-address or stride error in the dispatch rather than the kv_head term specifically. Suggested comment wording: "Each head carries its own offset (i / head_size), so the packer must read every head from its own address: a start pointer or stride that lands on the wrong head cannot pass (the fake pack copies the pointed-at values in order). Every value is exact in bf16."

kept.title: The PR body's "The linker rewrites both to the same code" and the Short version's "the kv_mul-4 kernels emit the same instructions as on main" are wider than the object compare shows for the PV kernel.
kept.body: Rule: a PR-body claim must not be wider than the evidence it cites (claim check). The Verification table says the 4-head PV kernel "differs only in how the thread-local scratch is addressed (main local-dynamic, branch general-dynamic, the register and offset differences follow from it). The linker rewrites both to the same code", and the Short version says "the kv_mul-4 kernels emit the same instructions as on main". The cited raw files (exec/results/glimmer-20261016/local-obj-compare/main-weights_times_v_128x4.s vs r2-4-weights_times_v_128x4.s) differ in 60 of 122 lines. The TLS sequence is 2 of those lines (`lea 0x0(%rip),%rdi; call` vs the `data16`-prefixed general-dynamic pair). The rest are register-allocation differences through the whole tile loop, for example main `mov $0x80,%edx; tileloadd (%rcx,%rdx,1),%tmm4; mov $0x200,%eax; tileloadd (%r14,%rax,1),%tmm5` vs branch `mov $0x80,%esi; tileloadd (%rax,%rsi,1),%tmm4; mov $0x200,%ecx; tileloadd (%r14,%rcx,1),%tmm5`, and the tilestored lines use %rax vs %rcx as the stride register. A linker relaxes only the TLS access sequence (GD or LD to LE); it does not rename registers, so the linked 4-head PV functions are equivalent but not the same bytes, and no post-link compare is in the PR. The cause is the one in the source: the thread_local P at this line is now a static local of a function template [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:284], which gives it vague linkage and the general-dynamic model. Proposed fix (wording only): in the Verification table replace "The linker rewrites both to the same code" with "The linker relaxes both TLS sequences to the same local-exec access; the remaining differences are register names in the tile loop, with the same instruction sequence", and in the Short version replace "the kv_mul-4 kernels emit the same instructions as on main" with "the kv_mul-4 pack and QK kernels are instruction-identical to main, and the PV kernel differs only in register names and its thread-local access sequence".
kept.rule: PR-body claim wider than the cited evidence (claim check)
kept.evidence:
284:  alignas(64) thread_local uint16_t P[TILE_ROWS_16][PAGE_TOKENS_64] = {};
PR body (Verification, Object compare row weights_times_v_128x4): "differs only in how the thread-local scratch is addressed (main local-dynamic, branch general-dynamic, the register and offset differences follow from it). The linker rewrites both to the same code"
PR body (Short version): "the kv_mul-4 kernels emit the same instructions as on main"
local-obj-compare diff main vs r2-4 PV: `tileloadd (%rcx,%rdx,1),%tmm4` vs `tileloadd (%rax,%rsi,1),%tmm4`; `tilestored %tmm0,(%rbx,%rax,1)` vs `tilestored %tmm0,(%rbx,%rcx,1)`
corrections: The count in the comment is off: the two PV files differ in 66 of 122 lines (diff reports 66 '<' and 66 '>' lines), not 60. Also add the supporting fact for the proposed wording: a mnemonic-only diff of the two files differs in only the 2 TLS lines, so "the same instruction sequence, different register names" is exactly what the raw files show.

Two facts to adjust before posting. (1) The listings differ in 66 of 122 lines per side, not 60 (diff main-weights_times_v_128x4.s r2-4-weights_times_v_128x4.s). (2) Say that the opcode-mnemonic sequence of the two PV listings is identical (0 mnemonic differences, 44 tileloadd/tilestored/tdpbf16ps each); only operands differ (TLS prologue, offsets, register names). So the Short version's "emit the same instructions" is defensible at the mnemonic level and is already qualified in the Verification table; narrow the finding's main point to the sentence "The linker rewrites both to the same code", which the pre-link object listings cannot show and which is not literally true after LD/GD-to-LE relaxation (register names and the two access sequences stay different). Keep the proposed replacement wording for that sentence; the Short-version rewording is optional.

Keep the finding, but change the proposed Verification-table wording so it does not replace one unmeasured linker claim with another. Suggested row text: "differs in the thread-local access sequence (main local-dynamic, branch general-dynamic, because the scratch is now a static local of a function template) and in register names through the tile loop; the mnemonic sequence is identical except the 2 TLS lines (120 of 122). Expected, not measured: the linker relaxes both to local-exec when the kernel is linked into the executable; no post-link compare was run." Short-version replacement stays as proposed: "the kv_mul-4 pack and QK kernels are instruction-identical to main, and the PV kernel differs only in register names and its thread-local access sequence".

kept.title: Two stacked header comments sit above all five using-declarations, so the line about "the two group sizes" also reads as describing HEAD_SIZE_128, PAGE_TOKENS_64 and TILE_ROWS_16.
kept.rule: comment describes the code it sits on
corrections: Keep the comment as posted. Optional precision for the reviewer: say the group lines must stay first (clang-format sorts consecutive using-declarations, "GROUP_HEADS_16" < "GROUP_HEADS_4" < "HEAD_SIZE_128"), so the fix is to name the two constants in the sentence, as proposed, rather than to move the comment or reorder the lines.

kept.title: The ROWS_PER_LANE_4 comment restates the lane-to-column claim already made at lines 152-153 of the same comment block.
kept.rule: comment economy: one claim stated once
kept.evidence:
152:// 64-bit pairs), 128-bit lane `lane` (0..3) of u[row_group][k] holds tile
153:// column 4 * lane + k for the four tokens 4 * row_group .. 4 * row_group + 3.
165:// A 128-bit lane holds 4 fp32 values: lane `lane` of u[.][0..3] holds tile
166:// columns 4 * lane .. 4 * lane + 3, which become 4 consecutive output rows.
167:constexpr size_t ROWS_PER_LANE_4 = 4;
corrections: The body's sentence "The reader checks whether the two sentences differ and finds they do not" is slightly overstated: lines 165-166 add one fact ("A 128-bit lane holds 4 fp32 values"), and the clause "which become 4 consecutive output rows" restates HEAD line 154 ("Output row 4 * lane + k ... is assembled from lane `lane` of u[0..3][k]"), not lines 152-153 alone. Suggested wording: "Lines 165-166 repeat the lane-to-column mapping of lines 152-153 and the column-to-output-row mapping of line 154; the only new fact is that a 128-bit lane holds 4 fp32 values."

The body should cite lines 152-155, not only 152-153: the "which become 4 consecutive output rows" half of lines 165-166 repeats lines 154-155 ("Output row 4 * lane + k ... is assembled from lane `lane` of u[0..3][k]"), while the column mapping repeats lines 152-153.

judged.title: The fakes and the real kernels are now both weak COMDAT symbols, so a duplicate definition would no longer fail the link.
judged.body: Check: ODR / link behaviour of the test TU that defines fakes of the primary templates. Before this PR the three kernels were ordinary functions: the test TU's fakes and amx_attn.o's definitions were both strong, so if amx_attn.o were ever pulled from libtron.a (tron is STATIC [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:187]) the link would fail with a duplicate definition. At HEAD the real kernels are explicit instantiation definitions [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:333-354] and the fakes are implicit instantiations of the primary templates the test TU defines [t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:253-284]. Both are emitted as weak COMDAT symbols. I verified this with a scratch pair of files under g++ (`nm` shows binding `W` for the explicit instantiations, and linking both objects directly succeeds with no error; the first object on the link line wins). judged.title: The PR body names the stage-3/stage-4 shuffle "vshufps"; the code uses _mm512_shuffle_f32x4, which is VSHUFF32X4, a different instruction with a different selector meaning.
judged.body: PR-body check (section "How to review this PR", question 1, first bullet): "row `4*l + k` of `s` uses the `vshufps` selector `0x88` when bit 0 of `l` is 0 and `0xdd` when it is 1." The code at HEAD [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:178-181] calls `_mm512_shuffle_f32x4(u[0][k], u[1][k], pair_sel)` and `_mm512_shuffle_f32x4(p, q2, quad_sel)`. That intrinsic compiles to VSHUFF32X4 (shuffle of 128-bit lanes). VSHUFPS (`_mm512_shuffle_ps`) shuffles 32-bit elements inside each 128-bit lane, and its 8-bit immediate selects elements, not lanes. With VSHUFPS the selector values 0x88 and 0xdd would not mean "even lanes" and "odd lanes", so a reviewer who looks up vshufps to check the selector reasoning reaches the wrong table. The object-compare row in [Verification] hedges with "40 `vshuf` shuffles", which is consistent with either name. Proposed fix in the PR body: replace "the `vshufps` selector" with "the `_mm512_shuffle_f32x4` (VSHUFF32X4, 128-bit lane shuffle) selector".

The comment [t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:142-143] says: "Each head carries its own offset (i / head_size), so a pack that permutes or drops heads cannot pass". In this translation unit the pack is the fake at lines 257-264, which copies `input[0 .. group_heads * HEAD_SIZE_128)` into `probe.q` in order; no real packer runs, so a permuting pack is not a break this file can see. A dropping pack is caught without the offset: a missing head leaves `probe.q[i]` at 0, and every `expected[i]` is at least 1.0. What the offset does add is a check on the pointer the dispatch passes [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1697: `q.data + kv_head * geometry.kv_mul() * geometry.kv.head_size`]: with the old fill `1.0f + (i % 4) * 0.25f`, a pointer offset by a whole head reads values identical to the expected ones, so the assertion at line 237 could not fail; with the per-head offset it fails. The assertion is not vacuous, but the comment names the wrong component. Every value is exact in bf16."

(2) "with the old fill ... the assertion at line 237 could not fail" is not certain: a pointer offset by +128 makes the last head read past the job's group into the next job's qs_roped, whose content the test does not set; if that memory is zero the old fill already fails on the last head. judged.body: Rule: a PR-body claim must not be wider than the evidence it cites (claim check). The Verification table says the 4-head PV kernel "differs only in how the thread-local scratch is addressed (main local-dynamic, branch general-dynamic, the register and offset differences follow from it). The linker rewrites both to the same code", and the Short version says "the kv_mul-4 kernels emit the same instructions as on main". The cited raw files (exec/results/glimmer-20261016/local-obj-compare/main-weights_times_v_128x4.s vs r2-4-weights_times_v_128x4.s) differ in 60 of 122 lines. The TLS sequence is 2 of those lines (`lea 0x0(%rip),%rdi; call` vs the `data16`-prefixed general-dynamic pair). The rest are register-allocation differences through the whole tile loop, for example main `mov $0x80,%edx; tileloadd (%rcx,%rdx,1),%tmm4; mov $0x200,%eax; tileloadd (%r14,%rax,1),%tmm5` vs branch `mov $0x80,%esi; tileloadd (%rax,%rsi,1),%tmm4; mov $0x200,%ecx; tileloadd (%r14,%rcx,1),%tmm5`, and the tilestored lines use %rax vs %rcx as the stride register. A linker relaxes only the TLS access sequence (GD or LD to LE); it does not rename registers, so the linked 4-head PV functions are equivalent but not the same bytes, and no post-link compare is in the PR. The cause is the one in the source: the thread_local P at this line is now a static local of a function template [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:284], which gives it vague linkage and the general-dynamic model. Proposed fix (wording only): in the Verification table replace "The linker rewrites both to the same code" with "The linker relaxes both TLS sequences to the same local-exec access; the remaining differences are register names in the tile loop, with the same instruction sequence", and in the Short version replace "the kv_mul-4 kernels emit the same instructions as on main" with "the kv_mul-4 pack and QK kernels are instruction-identical to main, and the PV kernel differs only in register names and its thread-local access sequence".

kept.title: The six explicit instantiations spell the two fixed page-view types four more times; one alias per view in the interface header would define the kernels' K-page and V-page operand types once.
kept.body:
Rule: ben-review, "repeated low-level representation details" and "Establish the shared concept" (the reference example in the skill is the same shape of fix: Ben's const_v_row_view alias in PR 4697).

Evidence (HEAD, amx_attn.cpp:335-354):
```
335 template void qk_rowmajor_128x4<GROUP_HEADS_4>(
336     const_native_k_view<PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128>,
...
340 template void qk_rowmajor_128x4<GROUP_HEADS_16>(
341     const_native_k_view<PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128>,
...
345 template void weights_times_v_128x4<GROUP_HEADS_4>(
346     v_vnni_view<const bf16, PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128>,
...
350 template void weights_times_v_128x4<GROUP_HEADS_16>(
351     v_vnni_view<const bf16, PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128>,
```
The same two spellings also sit on the declarations (amx_attn_iface.hpp:244, 259) and the definitions (amx_attn.cpp:193, 267). Counted with grep: amx_attn.cpp had 2 of these spellings at BASE and has 6 at HEAD; the four files together have 11.

Concept: "the K plane of one 64-token page as the QK kernel reads it" and "the packed V plane of one page as the PV kernel reads it". Both are fixed properties of the kernel shape (PAGE_TOKENS_64 x HEAD_SIZE_128, read-only bf16). Nothing varies between the occurrences.

Reading cost: each of the four new instantiation blocks is 4 to 5 lines that the reader must compare with the declaration in the header to confirm it names the same function. The only intended difference is GROUP_HEADS_4 against GROUP_HEADS_16, and it is on the first line. The element type, the page shape and the const-ness are repeated noise around that one decision.

Proposed fix (header, next to the shape constants, after group_heads_ok):
```cpp
// The page planes the kernels read: one 64-token page's native K plane (QK)
// and its packed V plane (PV), both read-only bf16.
using k_page_view = const_native_k_view<PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128>;
using v_page_view = v_vnni_view<const bf16, PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128>;
```
Then the declarations, definitions and instantiations use the names, for example:
```cpp
template void qk_rowmajor_128x4<GROUP_HEADS_4>(
    k_page_view, const bf16*, float*, size_t) noexcept;
template void qk_rowmajor_128x4<GROUP_HEADS_16>(

judged.title: The unpacked-tile register array is spelled two ways, as `__m512 u[4][4]` at its definition and as `__m512 (&u)[TILE_ROWS_16 / ROWS_PER_LANE_4][ROWS_PER_LANE_4]` at the new helper's parameter; one local alias would define that shape once.
judged.body:
Rule: ben-review, "callers repeatedly assembling that concept from generic machinery" (dimensions) and "compare near-identical expressions for intentional differences".

Evidence (HEAD):
```
170 inline void store_transposed_rows(
171     const __m512 (&u)[TILE_ROWS_16 / ROWS_PER_LANE_4][ROWS_PER_LANE_4],
...
233     __m512 u[4][4];
...
255     store_transposed_rows<0>(u, s_block, s_stride_floats);
```
The helper and its parameter type are new in this PR. The definition `__m512 u[4][4]` is pre-existing (BASE has the same line).

Concept: the 16 x 16 score tile after the two unpack stages, held as 4 row groups x 4 registers. One object, now described by two different expressions.

Reading cost: at line 255 the reader must work out that `TILE_ROWS_16 / ROWS_PER_LANE_4` is 4 to see that the reference parameter binds to `u`. The compiler enforces the match, so this is a reading cost, not a defect.

Proposed fix, in the anonymous namespace next to the helper:

// The 16 x 16 score tile after the two unpack stages: 4 row groups x 4
// registers, one per output row of the row group.
using unpacked_tile = __m512[TILE_ROWS_16 / ROWS_PER_LANE_4][ROWS_PER_LANE_4];

template <int lane>
inline void store_transposed_rows(
    const unpacked_tile& u, float* s_block, size_t s_stride_floats) {
```
and at line 233 `unpacked_tile u;`. The loop bounds at lines 231 and 236 (`< 4`) are unchanged by the diff and can stay.

judged.title: Pre-existing, for the issue #5021 follow-up: the score buffer is described by three separate items (float* s, size_t s_stride_floats, and now the group_heads template argument) where a typed 2-D view would carry rows, columns and stride in one type, as the K operand already does.
judged.body:
Rule: ben-review, "Several values describing one concept, such as a buffer's pointer and length" and "Judge limitations against the baseline". This is explicitly pre-existing: the runtime parameter lists are unchanged at HEAD, and the commit message keeps them unchanged on purpose. The diff adds the third item (the template row count), so the triple is newly complete, not newly introduced. Reported as fwiw for the follow-up that issue #5021 tracks ("a future shape is a minimal code change"), not as a change request on this PR.

Evidence (HEAD):
```
242 template <size_t group_heads>
243   requires(group_heads_ok(group_heads))
244 void qk_rowmajor_128x4(const_native_k_view<PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> k_page,
245     const bf16* q_packed,
246     float* s,
247     size_t s_stride_floats) noexcept;
```
and the same pair on the PV kernel (`const float* exp_rows, size_t row_stride_floats`, lines 260-261). The comment at line 237 already describes the concept in one expression: "s[group_heads][s_stride_floats] fp32".

At the call site the caller rebuilds that concept from a typed tensor and then pins the relation with a static_assert (self_attention.hpp):
```
1756       tensor<operation_kv_mul, page::page_size> s_pages;
1760       static_assert(
1761           sizeof(s_pages) == operation_kv_mul * page::page_size * sizeof(float),
1762           "the AMX kernels read s_pages as one block: rows must be consecutive");
1763       amx_attn_h128g4::qk_rowmajor_128x4<operation_kv_mul>(
1764           pg.template k<geometry.kv>(slot, kv_head), q_packed, &s_pages[0][0],
1765           page::page_size);
```

Reading cost: at each of the two kernel calls the reader relates the template argument to the tensor's row count and the stride argument to its column count, and reads the static_assert to learn why the pointer form is safe. The K operand on the same call shows the alternative: `const_native_k_view<Rows, Cols>` (kv_cache_fwd.hpp:49-54) is a `const_view` whose shape and stride are in the type.

Possible follow-up shape (not for this PR): a `view<float, VIEW_ALIGNED_TRUE, VIEW_DMA_FALSE, seq<group_heads, PAGE_TOKENS_64>, sseq<PAGE_TOKENS_64, 1>>` parameter for `s` and for `exp_rows`, taken from `s_pages`, would make the row count, column count and stride one object, remove the stride argument, and let the static_assert at 1760-1762 go. The difference that must survive: the kernel would then fix the column count at 64, which the comment at line 237 ("all 64 token columns") already states.

judged.rule: ben-review: properties derivable from supplied values are inferred, not restated; the finder's 'group-size set stated twice' check
corrections: If the author still wants to post it: drop the "finder's two-places check" and "third place that encodes the group-size set" claims (neither is in the ben-review skill, and line 256 tests one member, it does not restate the set). Keep the finding; adjust the comment text before posting. (1) Remove the finder-process narration ("the finder's own check ... stated as clean", "it is reported because ...") since a PR reader has no finder; state only the rule, the evidence and the fix. (2) The repo ColumnLimit is 88, not 90 (.clang-format line 85). The proposed `static_assert(group_heads % ROWS_PER_LANE_4 == 0, "each stored lane is 4 query rows");` line is 90 columns at 4-space indent and will be wrapped by clang-format; either accept the wrap or shorten the message. Also place the static_assert and `constexpr size_t lanes` at the top of qk_rowmajor_128x4 (before the `for (int r ...)` loop at line 231), not inside the loop body where the finder's snippet puts them. (4) Name the two texts that need the matching edit: the comment at amx_attn.cpp:227-230 ("only when group_heads is 16") and the PR body sentence "Lanes 1 to 3 exist only in the 16-head instantiation". (5) Say explicitly that the current code is correct under the requires clause at line 209, so this is a derivation/readability nit, not a defect.
refutations:
Scope (a) holds: lines 255-260 of src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp are new in this diff (BASE has only the inline lane-0 shuffle sequence at its lines 210-213, no store_transposed_rows, no group_heads). The finding fails on (b) and (c).

(b) The cited rule does not support it. The ben-review skill's table row reads "Properties derivable from supplied values or types: Infer where the language permits", and the section it sits in is about callers "repeatedly assembling that concept from generic machinery: template arguments, flags, dimensions, strides, or construction steps". HEAD line 256 `if constexpr (group_heads == GROUP_HEADS_16) {` supplies nothing redundantly. It is one branch on the single template parameter, so there is no derivable property restated beside its source. The finding's other justification, "the finder's own check 'the group-size set stated twice'", is not a rule in the skill file (no such check exists in ~/.claude/skills/ben-review/SKILL.md). The line also does not state the group-size set a third time. It tests one member of it. The set is bounded by `requires(group_heads_ok(group_heads))` on the same kernel at HEAD line 192, which the reader sees in the function header. The skill's calibration section cuts the other way: "Do not hide meaningful differences or add options for hypothetical callers" and "repetition alone does not justify another abstraction". The proposed `lanes > 1/2/3` form still enumerates lanes 1..3 by hand, so it removes no enumeration, and its only concrete gain is correct behavior for a group size that group_heads_ok does not accept (8). That is generality for a hypothetical caller.

The claimed reading cost is already paid by the diff. HEAD lines 227-230 state both facts the finding says the reader must look up: "Transpose s_transposed(64x16) -> s rows 0..group_heads-1 only" and "the store helper emits stages 3 and 4 for lane 0 (rows 0..3) always and for lanes 1..3 (rows 4..15) only when group_heads is 16."

(c) The PR body answers it. Line 29 documents the design: "Lane 0 is the sequence the 4-head kernel runs on main, at the same addresses. Lanes 1 to 3 exist only in the 16-head instantiation (`if constexpr`)." Line 123 defers "the requirement that a future shape is a minimal code change" to issue #5021, and the finding itself admits the overlap ("the author may defer it there"). judged.title: The QK sentinel buffer names its row count GROUP_HEADS_16 while its role is "every row a tile store could write", which the same file spells TILE_ROWS_16 for the PV buffer.
judged.body: Rule: "Prefer a name that explains the object's role" and "compare near-identical expressions for intentional differences". Evidence at HEAD: line 174 `alignas(64) float s_amx[GROUP_HEADS_16][PAGE_TOKENS_64];` and line 210 `for (size_t qi = group_heads; qi < GROUP_HEADS_16; ++qi) {`, against line 267 `o_amx[TILE_ROWS_16 * HEAD_SIZE_128];  // See Note [Tile stores write 16 rows]`. Both buffers exist for the same reason, stated by the comment at 158-162: the kernel could touch up to the tile's 16 rows, and the test pins which of them it writes (Note [Tile stores write 16 rows]). The PV buffer says so with TILE_ROWS_16. The QK buffer says "the larger group size", so in the 4-head section the reader asks why a 4-head check is sized by the 16-head group, and has to find static_assert(GROUP_HEADS_16 == TILE_ROWS_16) in the header (amx_attn_iface.hpp:146-147) to see that the two names are the same number. In the dispatch test the same name is right (t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:63-64, "Room for the larger group", a Q buffer, not a tile output). Fix: at 174 `alignas(64) float s_amx[TILE_ROWS_16][PAGE_TOKENS_64];` and at 210 `for (size_t qi = group_heads; qi < TILE_ROWS_16; ++qi) {`. TILE_ROWS_16 is already imported at line 42.
judged.rule: ben-review: a name explains the object's role; the same concept spelled two ways in one file
corrections: Do not post. If posted anyway, drop the sentence "Both buffers exist for the same reason, stated by the comment at 158-162: the kernel could touch up to the tile's 16 rows" — the Note at amx_attn_iface.hpp:107-110 and the test comment at t_amx_numerics.cpp:158-162 say the QK kernel writes only group_heads rows of `s`; only `o` of weights_times_v_128x4 receives a 16-row tile store.
refutations: The line numbers are right (t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:174 `alignas(64) float s_amx[GROUP_HEADS_16][PAGE_TOKENS_64];`, :210 `for (size_t qi = group_heads; qi < GROUP_HEADS_16; ++qi) {`, :267 `o_amx[TILE_ROWS_16 * HEAD_SIZE_128];  // See Note [Tile stores write 16 rows]`), but the finding's premise is not true of the code. It says "Both buffers exist for the same reason, stated by the comment at 158-162: the kernel could touch up to the tile's 16 rows." The comment at 158-162 says the opposite for QK: "the kernel writes only the group_heads query rows, so `s` needs only group_heads rows (Note [Tile stores write 16 rows])." The Note itself (h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:107-110) states that qk_rowmajor_128x4 stores its tiles into an internal buffer (s_transposed, src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:201 and :223-226) and the transpose writes only group_heads rows into `s` (store_transposed_rows<1..3> guarded by `if constexpr (group_heads == GROUP_HEADS_16)`, amx_attn.cpp:255-260). The header also says "Only one caller buffer receives a tile store directly: the output `o` of weights_times_v_128x4" (amx_attn_iface.hpp:129-132). So o_amx is 16 rows because the kernel writes 16 rows by contract (role = tile rows), while s_amx is 16 rows because the templated test runs for both group sizes and checks that rows group_heads..15 are left untouched (role = room for the larger group, the same idiom as t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:63-64 "Room for the larger group"). Renaming s_amx to TILE_ROWS_16 would suggest `s` receives a tile store, which the Note explicitly denies. The finding's further claim that a reader "has to find static_assert(GROUP_HEADS_16 == TILE_ROWS_16)" to see the two are equal is also weak: both names carry the value in their _16 suffix. Not a defect, and the rule "a name explains the object's role" supports the current names.

The finding's premise is wrong: the QK score buffer `s` is not a buffer "a tile store could write", so TILE_ROWS_16 would be the misleading name, and GROUP_HEADS_16 is the role-explaining one.

(a) Scope: the lines are new in this diff (BASE t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:160 had `s_amx[GROUP_HEADS_4][PAGE_TOKENS_64]`; HEAD 174 and 210 use GROUP_HEADS_16), so the hunk is in scope. The refutation is on substance, not scope.

(b) Rule: ben-review SKILL.md:61 "Prefer a name that explains the object's role". The role of the 16 rows differs between the two buffers:
- PV output `o`: the header says the tile store lands in it directly. amx_attn_iface.hpp:128-132: "Only one caller buffer receives a tile store directly: the output `o` of weights_times_v_128x4. The caller must therefore allocate `o` with TILE_ROWS_16 rows, not group_heads." So TILE_ROWS_16 at t_amx_numerics.cpp:267 names that role.
- QK output `s`: no tile store reaches it. amx_attn.cpp:222-225 store the accumulator tiles into the kernel-local `s_transposed`; amx_attn.cpp:227-230 then do a transposing store "-> s rows 0..group_heads-1 only ... lanes 1..3 (rows 4..15) only when group_heads is 16". The test's own comment at t_amx_numerics.cpp:158-162 states the contrast: "the kernel writes only the group_heads query rows, so `s` needs only group_heads rows (Note [Tile stores write 16 rows])". The sentinel buffer has 16 rows so that one template body serves both instantiations (check_qk<GROUP_HEADS_4> at 321, check_qk<GROUP_HEADS_16> at 324) and proves rows group_heads..15 stay untouched up to the largest group's head index. That extent is the 16 packed-Q columns of the B tile = the larger group size (amx_attn_iface.hpp:143-145), which is exactly what GROUP_HEADS_16 names.

Renaming 174/210 to TILE_ROWS_16 would say "this buffer receives a tile store", contradicting amx_attn_iface.hpp:128-132 and the comment at 158-162. The two names are equal by static_assert (amx_attn_iface.hpp:146-147) but name different concepts; using the right one per buffer is not "the same concept spelled two ways". The same reasoning the finding accepts for t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:63-64 ("room for the larger group", not a tile output) applies here.

(c) Not covered by the PR body or issue #5021; refuted on (b) alone.

The finding rests on "both buffers exist for the same reason: the kernel could touch up to the tile's 16 rows". That is false for the QK score buffer. The header Note states at amx_attn_iface.hpp:107-110 that qk_rowmajor_128x4 tile-stores into its own internal buffer (s_transposed) and "the transpose that reads that buffer writes only the group_heads query rows into the caller's `s`", and at 129-132 that "Only one caller buffer receives a tile store directly: the output `o` of weights_times_v_128x4". The kernel confirms it: amx_attn.cpp:222-225 store the four result tiles into the local s_transposed[PAGE_TOKENS_64 * TILE_ROWS_16] (line 201), and the only path that could write rows 4..15 of `s` is the transposed-store lanes 1..3 that are emitted under `if constexpr (group_heads == GROUP_HEADS_16)` (amx_attn.cpp:254-259). In `s`, rows are query heads, and the AMX tile rows are tokens (four 16-token tiles), so TILE_ROWS_16 would name the wrong axis. The 16-row s_amx exists to catch the 16-head store lanes if the 4-head instantiation emitted them, i.e. "room for the larger group", which is exactly the role the finding accepts for the dispatch test's Q buffer (t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:63-64). The sentinel loop at t_amx_numerics.cpp:210 `for (size_t qi = group_heads; qi < GROUP_HEADS_16; ++qi)` reads as "this group's rows up to the largest group's rows" without consulting the static_assert; the comment at 158-162 already states that `s` needs only group_heads rows. The proposed fix would compile and keep tests green (same value, TILE_ROWS_16 imported at line 42), but it would be worse: it would suggest `s` receives a tile store, contradicting the Note at header lines 107-110 and 129-132, and would mis-label the head axis as the tile-row axis. The stated reading cost is hypothetical and does not merit a comment even at nit severity.

judged.title: For the issue #5021 follow-up: the Q-group operand is a bare pointer whose length is now set by the template argument, two items for one concept, where the K operand already has a typed view.

Evidence at HEAD: line 204 `void pack_q_group_128x4(const bf16* q_group, bf16* packed) noexcept;` under `template <size_t group_heads>` (202). The diff made the length of `q_group` depend on the template argument (group_heads x 128 bf16, comment at 187) while the parameter stays `const bf16*`. The K operand of the sibling kernel is `const_native_k_view<PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128>` (244), introduced "so that a packed V plane or a bare pointer cannot be handed in by mistake" (239-240). Callers now assemble the Q group's extent themselves: self_attention.hpp:1697 `q.data + kv_head * geometry.kv_mul() * geometry.kv.head_size`, t_amx_numerics.cpp:74 and 134 `group_heads * HEAD_SIZE_128`, t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:64 and 260. Reading cost: at the pack call the reader checks by hand that the template argument and the pointer's extent agree; a 4-head buffer passed to the 16-head instantiation reads 1536 bf16 (3 KiB) past the group and no type says so (the dispatch test guards it at t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:202). A view such as `q_group_view<group_heads>` (group_heads rows x 128 bf16, contiguous) would tie the extent to the instantiation at compile time, as const_native_k_view does for K. This is the same family as the confirmed s/s_stride_floats finding and is pre-existing in kind (the pointer was bare on main), so it is for #5021, not this PR; it is listed because the diff is what made the extent template-dependent.
judged.rule: ben-review: several values describing one concept (pointer plus length); reference example const_v_row_view
corrections: Minor wording only: t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:202 (`REQUIRE(probe.pack_group_heads == (packs ? n_heads : 0))`) checks that the instantiated group_heads equals the model's head count; it does not check the buffer extent, so "guards the mismatch indirectly, by checking the template argument matches n_heads" is more exact than "guards it".

If the text is reused for issue #5021: (1) `const_native_k_view` on the K operand was not "introduced" by this PR; it is at BASE amx_attn_iface.hpp:222. (2) The bare `const bf16* q_group` is at BASE line 187 unchanged; the diff only adds the template parameter. (3) Issue #5021 tracks the rename plus the minimal-change-for-new-shapes requirement; it does not mention a typed Q-group view, so the proposal would be a new item there, not a follow-up already tracked.
refutations: Pre-existing, unchanged in kind, and outside the rule's trigger. (a) Scope: at BASE amx_attn_iface.hpp:187 the declaration is already `void pack_q_group_128x4(const bf16* q_group, bf16* packed) noexcept;` with a bare pointer whose extent (4 x 128 bf16) lived only in the comment; the diff adds `template <size_t group_heads>` (HEAD 202-204) and leaves the pointer as it was. The K operand's typed view is also not introduced by this PR: BASE line 222 already reads `void qk_rowmajor_128x4(const_native_k_view<PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> k_page, ...`. The callers' extent arithmetic is unchanged too: BASE self_attention.hpp:1697 already has `q.data + kv_head * geometry.kv_mul() * geometry.kv.head_size`, BASE t_amx_numerics.cpp:122 `q[GROUP_HEADS_4 * HEAD_SIZE_128]`. The diff does not worsen the reading cost: at BASE the reader matched the pointer's extent against a comment constant, at HEAD against a visible template argument, and the one production caller takes both the template argument `<geometry.kv_mul()>` and the offset from the same `geometry.kv_mul()` (HEAD self_attention.hpp:1696-1697), so they cannot disagree there. The finder itself states "pre-existing in kind (the pointer was bare on main)". The ben-review skill says "Do not report pre-existing smells as new findings or use this review to recommend unrelated cleanup" and "Do not describe an unchanged missing check as a weakness introduced by a refactor." (b) Rule: the quoted bullet "Several values describing one concept, such as a buffer's pointer and length" is listed under "Investigate more than four parameters" as a question to ask of a long parameter list; pack_q_group_128x4 has two runtime parameters and one template parameter, and no length parameter at all. The finding is a readability wish, not a defect: the finder concedes the mis-sized case is guarded by t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:202 and no caller passes a mismatched extent. (c) Exclusion: the finding routes itself to issue #5021 ("so it is for #5021, not this PR"); #5021 (read via gh) tracks the rename and the minimal-change-for-a-new-shape requirement, and the PR body line 123 already defers that follow-up. A finding whose own text says it is not for this PR is not a PR 5015 finding.

The rule quoted ("several values describing one concept, such as a buffer's pointer and length") covers two runtime arguments that must agree. At HEAD amx_attn_iface.hpp:202-204 the signature carries one runtime value; the extent is the template argument `group_heads`, a compile-time constant of the instantiation. That is exactly the property a fixed-size view gives: const_view<..., seq<group_heads, 128>> holds only `T const* data` (view.hpp:290-294), so a `q_group_view<group_heads>` would rename the pointer, not add a checked second quantity. The confirmed s/s_stride_floats finding is a different case (two runtime values).

The stated consequence is hypothetical at every HEAD call site. The only production caller (self_attention.hpp:1696-1697) takes the template argument and the pointer offset from the same `geometry.kv_mul()` constant on two adjacent lines, and `q` is `queries[tok_ix].as_view()` (1625), the token's full n_heads x 128 row, so the group's extent is the geometry's, not a separately tracked length. The test callers size their buffers with the same `group_heads` template parameter (t_amx_numerics.cpp:74 `tron::bf16 q[group_heads * HEAD_SIZE_128]`, :134 `alignas(64) tron::bf16 q[group_heads * HEAD_SIZE_128]`). A 4-head buffer handed to the 16-head instantiation would need a caller that picks the template argument independently of its buffer; none exists.

The proposed fix would not add compile-time safety. const_view is explicitly constructible from a bare pointer (view.hpp:291-293), so the production call would become `q_group_view<kv_mul>{q.data + kv_head * kv_mul * head_size}`: the same unchecked pointer arithmetic, one token longer. The K view is different in kind: it is produced by typed storage, `pg.template k<geometry.kv>(slot, kv_head)` (self_attention.hpp:1762), so the type travels from storage to kernel; no typed query-group sub-view exists at HEAD, so the new alias's only producer would be a pointer cast. The fix also changes the public fake (t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:257) and both numerics callers for no checking gain.

Finally, issue #5021 is the namespace/suffix rename; a typed-operand proposal does not belong under it. A comment marked "fwiw, not this PR" whose fix adds no safety is not worth posting on PR 5015.

composed.review_body:
ben-review: Short version. I checked the diff of PR 5015 (BASE 6198824246 to HEAD 5061623a34) for missing shared abstractions, repeated representation details and argument lists longer than four parameters, reading the full HEAD text of all six touched files. I found 6 items: 5 nits and 1 fwiw note for the issue #5021 follow-up, and no defect. Verdict for this reviewer: approve with nits.

All findings are inline comments.

comments.body:
ben-review: The four new explicit instantiations repeat the two page-view type spellings that the declarations and definitions already carry, so one shared alias per view would name each kernel operand type once [nit].

Evidence (HEAD lines 336 and 346, repeated at 341 and 351):
```
const_native_k_view<PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128>,
v_vnni_view<const bf16, PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128>,
```
Counted with grep: this file had 2 of these spellings at BASE and has 6 at HEAD. The four touched files together have 11.

Reading cost: each instantiation block is 4 to 5 lines, and the only intended difference is GROUP_HEADS_4 against GROUP_HEADS_16 (the two instantiated group sizes) on the first line.

The vocabulary already exists as local aliases in t/t_llama_unit.cpp:482-485 (`k_plane_t`, `v_plane_t`). Promoting them to the interface header next to the shape constants would define the concept once:
```cpp
// One 64-token page's native K plane (QK) and packed V plane (PV), read-only bf16.
using const_k_plane_view = const_native_k_view<PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128>;
using const_v_plane_view = v_vnni_view<const bf16, PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128>;
```
The aliases name existing types only. They add no guarantee and remove none. The column limit is 88, so the two-line instantiation form survives clang-format. The test spellings can stay as they are.

ben-review: The pack call spells `geometry.kv_mul()` (kv_mul = query heads per KV head) twice in two lines, once as the template argument and once in the pointer offset, where the sibling functions name that quantity once as `operation_kv_mul` [nit].

Evidence (HEAD):
```
1696         amx_attn_h128g4::pack_q_group_128x4<geometry.kv_mul()>(
1697             q.data + kv_head * geometry.kv_mul() * geometry.kv.head_size, slot);
```
The template argument at 1696 is new in this PR. The sibling `apply_dense_amx_page` already follows the one-name idiom:
```
1742       constexpr size_t operation_kv_mul = geometry.kv_mul();
1763       amx_attn_h128g4::qk_rowmajor_128x4<operation_kv_mul>(
1791       amx_attn_h128g4::weights_times_v_128x4<operation_kv_mul>(
```
The PR body states that both spellings are the model's kv_mul. This comment asks to make that visible in the code itself. Reading cost: the reader of `packed_amx_query` must confirm that the group size the kernel is instantiated for and the group stride of the pointer offset are the same quantity on purpose.

Proposed fix, inside `packed_amx_query` before the `if`:
```cpp
      constexpr size_t operation_kv_mul = geometry.kv_mul();
      if (!packed.test(batch_job_ix)) {
        amx_attn_h128g4::pack_q_group_128x4<operation_kv_mul>(
            q.data + kv_head * operation_kv_mul * geometry.kv.head_size, slot);
```
Behaviour is identical.

ben-review: Pre-existing, noted for the issue #5021 follow-up and not as a change request on this PR: the score buffer is described by three separate items (`float* s`, `size_t s_stride_floats`, and now the `group_heads` row count) where a typed 2-D view would carry rows, columns and stride in one type, as the K operand on the same call already does [fwiw].

Evidence (HEAD):
```
244 void qk_rowmajor_128x4(const_native_k_view<PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> k_page,
245     const bf16* q_packed,
246     float* s,
247     size_t s_stride_floats) noexcept;
```
The PV kernel carries the same pair (`exp_rows`, `row_stride_floats`, lines 260-261), and so does the new internal helper `store_transposed_rows` in amx_attn.cpp. The comment at line 237 already states the concept in one expression: "s[group_heads][s_stride_floats] fp32". The K operand shows the alternative: `const_native_k_view<Rows, Cols>` (h/tron/tensor/kv_cache_fwd.hpp:49-53) holds shape and stride in the type.

Reading cost: at each kernel call (self_attention.hpp:1763, 1791) the reader relates the template argument to the `s_pages` row count and the stride to its column count, plus the static_assert at 1760-1762.

Possible follow-up shape: a `view<float, ..., rows group_heads x PAGE_TOKENS_64, strides PAGE_TOKENS_64 x 1>` parameter (shorthand, not existing aliases). Three things to carry: the static_assert stays unless a 2-D tensor-to-view conversion derives the stride, the kernels use unaligned loads and stores so VIEW_ALIGNED_TRUE promises more than needed, and the test fakes (t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:265-285) and requires-probes (t_llama_unit.cpp:96-105) bind the exact parameter types.

ben-review: The three new group-size assertions compare against `n_heads`, where the concept is the model's kv_mul (query heads per KV head) and `geometry.kv_mul()` already names it in this test [nit].

Evidence (HEAD lines 202-204):
```
    REQUIRE(probe.pack_group_heads == (packs ? n_heads : 0));
    REQUIRE(probe.qk_group_heads == (dense ? n_heads : 0));
    REQUIRE(probe.pv_group_heads == (dense ? n_heads : 0));
```
The production call sites pass the group size as `geometry.kv_mul()` and `operation_kv_mul` (self_attention.hpp:1696, 1763, 1791). This test already holds that value: line 84 builds `geometry` from `n_heads` and `n_kv_heads`, and `n_heads` equals the group size only because line 82 sets `n_kv_heads = 1`. The comment at 77-78 ("with one KV head it is also the AMX group size") exists to carry that condition.

Reading cost: at each REQUIRE the reader must recall that condition, and a later test shape with 2 KV heads would make the three lines wrong without any edit to them.

Proposed fix, right after line 84 (the alias reads `geometry`):
```cpp
  constexpr size_t group_heads = geometry.kv_mul();
```
used in the three REQUIREs. The comment at 77-78 then keeps "`n_heads` is the model's query head count" and drops the clause about the group size. Optional follow-on, outside the diff: line 156 `facts.kv_mul = n_heads / n_kv_heads;` could become `facts.kv_mul = group_heads;`. Test-local name, kept local.

The sibling gate eleven lines below reads `constexpr bool shape_ok(size_t model_head_size, size_t model_kv_mul) noexcept {` [h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:163], and both call sites pass a spelled name: `group_heads_ok(model_kv_mul)` [:164] and `requires(group_heads_ok(group_heads))` [:203, :243, :257]. The one-letter `g` is the only abbreviated parameter in the header. Wade's precedent is 2897235803 (gof_configure `nk, nh, hs` renamed to full names). Nit, never blocking. Proposed replacement for line 152:

```suggestion

```

kept.rule: Wade check 20 (identifier states its role)
refutations: Lens (a) passes: line 152 `constexpr bool group_heads_ok(size_t g) noexcept {` is new in this diff (BASE has no group_heads_ok; BASE amx_attn_iface.hpp:149 only has shape_ok). Lens (c) passes: the PR body line 34 names group_heads_ok but says nothing about its parameter name. Lens (b) fails, which refutes the finding. Wade check 20's trigger is "abbreviates a repository spelling", its procedure step 3 is "`git grep -w -c` both spellings at BASE. Report a finding when one spelling has ten times the hits of the other", and its do-not-fire list opens with "tokens with ten or more BASE hits" [~/.claude/skills/Wade-code-review/SKILL.md:208, :213, :217]. At BASE (h/ and src/), the token `g` has 304 word hits and `group_heads` has 0 hits (the name is introduced by this PR); `kv_mul` has 23. So there is no repository spelling that `g` abbreviates, the ten-times ratio runs in the opposite direction from the check (the short form is the common token), and `g` itself has far more than ten BASE hits, which the skill lists as a do-not-fire condition. The cited precedent 2897235803 had the opposite counts (full names 202/92/383 vs abbreviations 0/0/4 [references/procedures.md:158]), so it does not transfer. The finding is a style preference not supported by the named check. Note the HEAD quote is accurate: lines 152-153 read `constexpr bool group_heads_ok(size_t g) noexcept {` / `  return g == GROUP_HEADS_4 || g == GROUP_HEADS_16;`, and `g` appears only on those two lines in the two AMX files.

kept.title: check_qk and check_pv are new 50- and 80-line helpers with no comment at their declaration; only the TEST_CASE names 150 lines below say what they check.

kept.title: `inline` on store_transposed_rows changes nothing: it is a function template inside an anonymous namespace.
kept.body: Wade-code-review check 22 (redundant specifier), his 'a bit pedantic but' form (2976643305). HEAD line 170 reads `inline void store_transposed_rows(` under `template <int lane>` [:169], inside the `namespace {` opened at :148 and closed at :185. A function template is already exempt from the one-definition rule, and the anonymous namespace already gives it internal linkage, so deleting `inline` changes no linkage, no type and no build. The PR body's object compare shows the 4-head QK kernel instruction-identical to main, so the specifier did not decide inlining either. fwiw only; no action needed.
kept.rule: Wade check 22 (redundant statement, member, branch, specifier or scope)
kept.evidence:
148: namespace {
169: template <int lane>
170: inline void store_transposed_rows(
185: }  // namespace
corrections: One wording nit before posting: the object compare shows that the function WAS inlined (the 4-head kernel is instruction-identical to main, where the store was written in place), but by itself it does not show that the `inline` specifier played no part in that decision. The stronger argument is structural: each instantiation `store_transposed_rows<0..3>` has a single call site [amx_attn.cpp:255, :257-259] inside an internal-linkage kernel, and clang at -O3 inlines such called-once internal functions regardless of the specifier. Suggest replacing "so the specifier did not decide inlining either" with "and each instantiation has a single call site [:255, :257-259], which clang at -O3 inlines regardless of the specifier".

Minor wording: "A function template is already exempt from the one-definition rule" is loose. The precise statement is that the one-definition rule already allows a function template to be defined in every translation unit, the same allowance `inline` grants a plain function; and the anonymous namespace makes the point moot by giving the template internal linkage. Optionally add that `detect_and_request` at HEAD line 86, the file's other anonymous-namespace function, carries no `inline`, so dropping it also matches the file's own idiom.

Replace "The PR body's object compare shows the 4-head QK kernel instruction-identical to main, so the specifier did not decide inlining either." with: "The specifier is not needed for inlining either: the body is a four-iteration shuffle loop, which -O3 inlines with or without the hint, and the PR body's object compare shows it folded into qk_rowmajor_128x4 (205 instructions, identical to main). The rest of the file agrees: detect_and_request() at :56 in the first anonymous namespace carries no inline, and :170 is the only inline function in amx_attn.cpp."

kept.title: The QK store branch keys on group_heads == 16 and silently treats every other size as 4 heads; nothing names that assumption.
kept.body: Check 27 (silent fallback where an assert belongs). The transposing store always runs lane 0 and adds lanes 1..3 only under one equality test: `store_transposed_rows<0>(u, s_block, s_stride_floats);` (src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:255) and `if constexpr (group_heads == GROUP_HEADS_16) {` (:256). The two other kernels are generic on the parameter: the pack loop is `for (size_t q_head = 0; q_head < group_heads; q_head++) {` (:138) and the P loop is `for (size_t q = 0; q < group_heads; q++) {` (:285). So only the QK store encodes "not 16 means 4". Today a bug-free caller cannot reach the implicit else with anything but 4: `requires(group_heads_ok(group_heads))` (:192) and `group_heads_ok` (h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:152-154) allow 4 and 16 only. If a third size were added to `group_heads_ok` (issue #5021 asks that a future shape be a minimal change), all three kernels would compile, pack and PV would serve the new size, and the QK kernel would write rows 0..3 of `s` only. The PV kernel would then read stale rows of `s_pages` for the other heads, and nothing would report it. Should the branch state its assumption so a third size fails to compile at this line? One form: `} else { static_assert(group_heads == GROUP_HEADS_4, "lane 0 stores rows 0..3, the 4-head case"); }`. Another: run lanes `< group_heads / ROWS_PER_LANE_4`. Nit, not blocking: unreachable at HEAD.
kept.rule: Wade-code-review check 27 (silent fallback where an assert belongs)
corrections: Replace "nothing names that assumption" with "only the comment at lines 247-250 names that assumption; nothing enforces it at compile time". The comment above the loop already says lanes 1..3 run only when group_heads is 16.

The finding should not be posted. If kept as a pure question, drop "nothing names that assumption" (the comment at amx_attn.cpp:227-230 and the requires clause at :192 name it) and drop the check 27 attribution, since the rule covers runtime guards a caller can reach, not a compile-time branch under a requires clause that admits exactly 4 and 16.

Replace "nothing names that assumption" / "So only the QK store encodes 'not 16 means 4'" with: the comment at src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:237-240 does name it in prose ("lanes 1..3 (rows 4..15) only when group_heads is 16"), but no compile-time check enforces it, so a third size added to group_heads_ok would compile and write rows 0..3 of s only. Keep the first fix form (else-branch static_assert); drop or demote the second form, since `lane` must stay a template argument (the shuffle selectors are immediates, :160-163), so a runtime lane loop would need an index-sequence helper. Note the static_assert message should be short enough for clang-format's 90 columns at 6-space indent (e.g. "lane 0 covers the 4-head case only"), or clang-format will wrap the string onto its own line, which is also acceptable.
refutations: Scope (a) holds: the `if constexpr (group_heads == GROUP_HEADS_16)` branch at src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:256 is new in this diff (BASE had one unconditional 0x88 store sequence at its lines 210-213). The finding fails on (b) and (c). (b) Check 27 reads: "Can a bug-free caller reach this? If not, why not assert, naming the value?" (SKILL.md:333-349). That assert already exists at compile time: `requires(group_heads_ok(group_heads))` on the kernel (amx_attn.cpp:192) and `group_heads_ok` returning `g == GROUP_HEADS_4 || g == GROUP_HEADS_16` (amx_attn_iface.hpp:152-154), with the comment "that file instantiates it for exactly this set" (iface:149-151). Any other group_heads fails to compile at :192 before the implicit else is ever instantiated. The title's claim "nothing names that assumption" is wrong: the comment at amx_attn.cpp:227-230 states "the store helper emits stages 3 and 4 for lane 0 (rows 0..3) always and for lanes 1..3 (rows 4..15) only when group_heads is 16", and :161-162 says "Lane 0 = (0x88, 0x88) is the one store sequence the 4-head kernel emits". Check 27's trigger list is runtime guards (clamp, silent exit, spin, sentinel) reachable by a caller; a compile-time branch under a requires clause that admits exactly two values, with no reachable third case, is not a silent fallback under that rule. (c) The only way to reach the implicit else is to edit `group_heads_ok` to add a third size; the finder itself ties that to "a future shape be a minimal change", which the PR body (pr-body.md:123) defers to issue #5021 and the task instructions exclude. The finder also concedes "unreachable at HEAD". The suggested static_assert would duplicate the requires clause one function above it.

kept.title: The 16-head QK and PV kernel sections never execute on the lane that gates this PR, and the only run that executed them is the author's local run.
kept.body:
Wade-code-review check 3A (a test must run, reach its assertion and observe the defect). Words used here: a lane is one CI workflow file with its trigger block and configure line. The gating lane is the workflow whose jobs `gh pr checks 5015 --required` lists.

kept.body: Check 6 (a claim wider than the code or the evidence). Line 3 says 'the kv_mul-4 kernels emit the same instructions as on main'. The Verification table at line 63 says of weights_times_v_128x4: 'differs only in how the thread-local scratch is addressed (main local-dynamic, branch general-dynamic, the register and offset differences follow from it). The linker rewrites both to the same code'. So of the three kernels, two objects are identical and one is not; the headline sentence covers all three. The clause that rescues it, 'The linker rewrites both to the same code', has no measurement behind it in the body: line 46 says the compare was done 'at -O3 on amx_attn.cpp ... outside the build system', i.e. on the object files, before linking. Also, general-dynamic-to-local-exec and local-dynamic-to-local-exec relaxations produce equivalent but not byte-identical sequences, so 'the same code' would need a linked-binary compare to stand. The cause is the template's static local at src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:284 ('alignas(64) thread_local uint16_t P[TILE_ROWS_16][PAGE_TOKENS_64] = {};'), which has vague linkage once the function is a template. Narrow the text or widen the evidence: 'the kv_mul-4 pack and QK kernels are instruction-identical to main; the PV kernel differs only in the thread-local addressing of its P scratch' in the Short version, and either drop 'The linker rewrites both to the same code' or add the compare of the linked runtron symbols that supports it.

Keep the problem; shorten the fix. Refuted on the rule lens (b), with the facts partly conceded.

(a) Scope: the sentence is new PR-body text for this head, so it is in scope. The code it rests on is real: src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:284 'alignas(64) thread_local uint16_t P[TILE_ROWS_16][PAGE_TOKENS_64] = {};' now sits inside 'template <size_t group_heads>' (amx_attn.cpp:264-266), while at BASE the same line (BASE amx_attn.cpp:232) was in a non-template function. No linked-binary compare exists in that result set, so 'The linker rewrites both to the same code' is indeed unmeasured.

(b) Rule: Wade check 6 (SKILL.md:631-646) triggers only on 'a body, commit, Note or doc sentence claiming (a) a compile-time type guarantee, (b) a timer or counter's scope, (c) a [0]-read container's count ..., or (d) a twice-stated default'. A summary of an object-code compare is none of the four subjects, and the check's finding shape ('`X` is only <timed | enforced> at <file:line>') does not fit it. The check also says 'Do not fire on: stated limitations', and the body states this limitation twice: pr-body.md:42 'the object compare in [Verification] (pack and QK identical, PV differs only in the thread-local access model)' and pr-body.md:63 (the full PV row). The Short version at line 3 is the summary those two lines qualify. The remaining substance (an unmeasured link-time sentence) is a measurement-method point, which the skill records as 'never more than a nit' (SKILL.md:854-866, 'Benchmark or measurement: 1 of 269 ... a wish'), not a should-fix.

(c) Body: the PV difference is answered at lines 42 and 63; the names are not involved.

So the finding is a plain-English/PR-description precision nit mislabelled as Wade check 6 at should-fix severity. If the author tightens the text anyway, the finder's proposed wording is accurate.

The nightly publish-deb run (schedule cron at publish-deb.yml:21-22) builds the package with `make deb` (publish-deb.yml:111), which configures with `cmake --preset deb` (GNUmakefile:510), and the deb preset sets "TRON_AMX_DISPATCH": "ON" (CMakePresets.json:68). So the nightly skips only the cmake-single-platform host-test lane; its deb contains the AMX kernels, and the PR body's "Performance at the CI configuration" section (lines 92-113) already measures that deb. The correct statement is: the required checks on this PR (GCP Nix) build without TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, so the AMX host tests of this PR run nowhere in CI; the kernels themselves reach CI only through the nightly deb perf phase after merge.

1. 'The only workflow that sets the option is cmake-single-platform.yml:355' is incomplete. The `deb` preset also sets it: CMakePresets.json:68 `"TRON_AMX_DISPATCH": "ON"`, and publish-deb.yml's build job produces gen-deb/tron_*_amd64.deb from that preset (publish-deb.yml:122) on its nightly schedule (publish-deb.yml:20-21). So the nightly deb on main does compile the kernels (which is why body line 98 can say the base deb's gate refuses Glimmer); what it never does for a PR is run the AMX test binaries, and no PR check builds a deb. Replace the sentence with: 'Outside the PR checks, the option is set only by cmake-single-platform.yml:355 (workflow_dispatch/workflow_call) and by the deb preset (CMakePresets.json:68) that the nightly publish-deb build on main uses.' 2. The proposed body sentence 'the rows above are the only runs of the kernels' is too narrow: the performance cells and the CI-configuration arms below are kernel runs too. Suggest instead, under 'Builds and tests': 'The PR's required checks (GCP Nix) build without TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, so they compile none of the AMX code and run the placeholder test cases. Every run of the kernels in this section is the author's run on delphi-3bda.' 3. Anchor the comment at body line 55 ('CI runs it'), the body's only CI sentence, not line 46, which the finder itself calls a correct measurement statement.
refutations:
Refuted on the rule (lens b) and on scope (lens a).

Rule: Wade check 7 fires only on an existing sentence. Its trigger reads "a sentence in the PR body ... has a CI subject ... it asserts a setting or coverage ... it is not about a build the author made (a named tree, machine or runtron arm is a measurement statement)" [~/.claude/skills/Wade-code-review/SKILL.md:648-653], and its finding shape opens with "'<quoted sentence>' names no lane" [SKILL.md:670]. The finder anchors on pr-body.md:46 ("Every result below comes from head 5061623a34 ... on delphi-3bda ... -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON") and itself says that line "is a measurement statement and fine". The finding then asks for a sentence that does not exist to be added. Check 7 verifies CI claims; it does not require a CI-coverage disclaimer. The only CI-subject sentences in the body are line 55 ("CI runs it", clang-format), which the finder confirms as correct and does not report, and lines 94/108 (the nightly perf phase shape and GitHub Actions run 38999609242), which assert no build setting and are not targeted. No sentence in the body claims the required checks executed the kernels, so the "reader who takes the 12 green required checks as execution of the 16-head kernels" is not a claim the body makes.

Scope: the gating facts the finder relies on are unchanged from BASE. CMakeLists.txt:46 defaults TRON_AMX_DISPATCH OFF at HEAD and at BASE 6198824246 (git show BASE:CMakeLists.txt line 46 identical). The `#ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` guards in h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp sit at 254, 276, 477, 1528, 1630, 1681 at HEAD and at the same lines at BASE. The placeholder cases exist at BASE too (BASE t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:284 and BASE t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:285, same TEST_CASE strings as HEAD :344 and :319). The nearest check that mentions a flag-off lane compiling a case out is 3A step 3 [SKILL.md:486], a test check with its own finding shape, and its do-not-fire list excludes exits present at BASE [SKILL.md:508]. The finder's workflow citations (cmake-single-platform.yml:355, publish-deb.yml:64-68, gcp-nix.yml on: push/pull_request/merge_group) are accurate, but they establish a pre-existing CI layout, not a defect this PR introduces or a claim its body makes.

kept.body: Check 6 (which code line reaches what the sentence says). Line 35 says 'the explicit instantiations at the end of the file: the same two sizes. A caller with any other size fails to link.' Each kernel declaration carries `requires(group_heads_ok(group_heads))` (h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:202-203, :242-243, :256-257), and group_heads_ok at :152-154 is true for 4 and 16 only. The sentence as written sends a reviewer to look for a link error that cannot happen. kept.title: The review guide names the instruction 'vshufps'; the code uses _mm512_shuffle_f32x4, which assembles to vshuff32x4.
kept.body: Check 6 (does each identifier in a claim sentence match the code line). Line 28 says 'row `4*l + k` of `s` uses the `vshufps` selector `0x88` when bit 0 of `l` is 0 and `0xdd` when it is 1'. The helper at src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:178-181 calls `_mm512_shuffle_f32x4`, whose instruction is VSHUFF32X4 (128-bit lane shuffle); VSHUFPS is a different instruction (32-bit element shuffle within 128-bit lanes) and would not implement the lane selection the comment at :155-160 describes. A reviewer who greps the disassembly for vshufps to verify the claim finds nothing; line 62 already counts '`vshuf` shuffles', which matches vshuff32x4. Suggested text: 'uses the `_mm512_shuffle_f32x4` (vshuff32x4) selector `0x88` ...'. The selector arithmetic itself checks out: after the unpack stages at :241-252, 128-bit lane l of u[row_group][k] holds tile column 4*l + k, and 0x88 picks lanes {0,2} and 0xdd lanes {1,3} of each input, so lane bit 0 drives stage 3 and bit 1 drives stage 4, writing row 4*lane + k at :176-181.

pr-body.md:28: 'In stage 3, row `4*l + k` of `s` uses the `vshufps` selector `0x88` when bit 0 of `l` is 0 and `0xdd` when it is 1. Stage 4 does the same with bit 1 of `l`.'
src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:178: '    __m512 p = _mm512_shuffle_f32x4(u[0][k], u[1][k], pair_sel);'
src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:181: '        s_rows + k * s_stride_floats, _mm512_shuffle_f32x4(p, q2, quad_sel));'
corrections: Change the rule citation from "Wade check 6 (claim sentence identifiers match the code)" to "Wade check 17 (comment, label or doc clause: does each identifier match the line it describes)". Check 6 covers type guarantees, timer/counter scope, [0]-read counts and twice-stated defaults, not instruction names.
