If re-homed under another reviewer: drop the "dead symbol" framing and the check 14/16 citations. `probe` is not dead at HEAD (readers at :186-237 and :258-282); it is unreferenced only in the TRON_AMX_DISPATCH-off build because every reader is an uninstantiated template. Keep the verified CI evidence (run 39064711603, job 117492574143, log line 1374) and the two fix options; both are consistent with HEAD (all amx_attn_h128g4 call sites in h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp sit under #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH at :254, :276, :477, :1528, :1630, :1681, :1872, so the fakes are unreferenced in an OFF build).

None of the facts need correcting. (c) The PR body does not mention the warning or the TRON_AMX_DISPATCH-off build of this test. (b) Neither named Wade check supports the finding. Check 14 (SKILL.md:84-99) fires on "zero hits" of `git grep -n -w NAME HEAD` minus the declaration; `probe` has readers at HEAD :186, :198-204, :236-237, :258-261, :271-272, :281-282, and the check's exclusion list says "Do not fire on: test-only helpers". Check 16 (SKILL.md:136-150) triggers on a flipped `#define` debug switch, an added dump/log/trace call, or an always-on debug print, and its exclusion list ends with "t/."; a compiler diagnostic emitted by the gating lane is none of its triggers, and the file is under t/. No Wade check mentions build warnings (grep -i warning on the skill file returns nothing). So the finding is refuted as a Wade-code-review item. The underlying fact (a new -Wunneeded-internal-declaration warning in the gating Build Tron lane, introduced by this PR) is real and verified; if the orchestrator wants it posted, it belongs to a reviewer or skill whose rules cover compiler warnings in CI lanes, not to Wade checks 14/16.

If re-filed under the plain-english skill (Rule 1, define at first use) rather than Wade check 9: replace ", our half" with the condition it stands for, without asserting the other half was idle. Safe wording: "on delphi-3bda (one of its two 4-card halves, socket 1; the other half is shared with another user and its load during these runs is not recorded)" or simply "on 4 cards of delphi-3bda (socket 1)". Do not write "with the other half idle" unless the raw results record that.

Replace the proposed fix. Do not delete ", our half": it is the condition that distinguishes the runtron cells (one socket) from the CI cells on "the whole of delphi-3bda" (line 96), and a reader comparing the tp4 rows of lines 77 and 113 needs it. Do not write "with the other half idle": the body has no record of what ran on the other socket, and the split exists because another user may use it. Suggested text for line 46: "on one socket of delphi-3bda (socket 1 of 2, NUMA node 1: 2 of its 8 FPGA cards for the tp2 cells, 4 for the tp4 cells; the other socket was not used by these runs)". Source of the numbers: exec/glimmer-20261016/campaign.sh lines 16, 79 and 80.
refutations: Lens (b) fails: Wade check 9 does not cover this phrase. The check's procedure (SKILL.md line 695) greps for exactly three things inside a Verification section: wall-clock times, machine-local paths and log names, and reconciliations between two revisions. Its bins (line 698) are the same three. The reader test (line 697) runs only "for each remaining hit" from that grep. pr-body.md:46 "on delphi-3bda, our half" is none of the three: no clock time, no /var/tmp or /home path or .log name, no N-vs-N reconciliation. The check's own do-not-fire list (line 700) keeps "a commit id plus a date that identifies the binary a result came from", which is what the rest of line 46 is. So the Wade rule yields no hit here; the finding is really a plain-English Rule 1 point (term not defined at first use), which is a different skill and not the rule named. Lens (a) and (c) do not rescue it: the body is new text in this PR, and the PR body's "Words used here" table (lines 15-22) does not define "our half", so the term is in fact undefined; but that makes it a candidate under the plain-english/PR-description skill, not Wade check 9. Also, the finder's proposed replacement "with the other half idle" is not a verified fact: the machine-sharing convention gives the other half to another user, who may have load on it during the runs; the body does not say the other half was idle.

judged.title: group_heads_ok names its parameter `g` while its sibling shape_ok spells its parameters out.
judged.body:
Wade-code-review check 20 (an identifier states its role). HEAD line 152 reads `constexpr bool group_heads_ok(size_t g) noexcept {`. The sibling gate eleven lines below reads `constexpr bool shape_ok(size_t model_head_size, size_t model_kv_mul) noexcept {` [h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:163], and both call sites pass a spelled name: `group_heads_ok(model_kv_mul)` [:164] and `requires(group_heads_ok(group_heads))` [:203, :243, :257]. The one-letter `g` is the only abbreviated parameter in the header. Wade's precedent is 2897235803 (gof_configure `nk, nh, hs` renamed to full names). Nit, never blocking. Proposed replacement for line 152:

```suggestion
constexpr bool group_heads_ok(size_t group_heads) noexcept {
```

and line 153 becomes `  return group_heads == GROUP_HEADS_4 || group_heads == GROUP_HEADS_16;`.
judged.rule: Wade check 20 (identifier states its role)
refutations: Lens (a) passes: line 152 `constexpr bool group_heads_ok(size_t g) noexcept {` is new in this diff (BASE has no group_heads_ok; BASE amx_attn_iface.hpp:149 only has shape_ok). Lens (c) passes: the PR body line 34 names group_heads_ok but says nothing about its parameter name. Lens (b) fails, which refutes the finding. Wade check 20's trigger is "abbreviates a repository spelling", its procedure step 3 is "`git grep -w -c` both spellings at BASE. Report a finding when one spelling has ten times the hits of the other", and its do-not-fire list opens with "tokens with ten or more BASE hits" [~/.claude/skills/Wade-code-review/SKILL.md:208, :213, :217]. At BASE (h/ and src/), the token `g` has 304 word hits and `group_heads` has 0 hits (the name is introduced by this PR); `kv_mul` has 23. So there is no repository spelling that `g` abbreviates, the ten-times ratio runs in the opposite direction from the check (the short form is the common token), and `g` itself has far more than ten BASE hits, which the skill lists as a do-not-fire condition. The cited precedent 2897235803 had the opposite counts (full names 202/92/383 vs abbreviations 0/0/4 [references/procedures.md:158]), so it does not transfer. The finding is a style preference not supported by the named check. Note the HEAD quote is accurate: lines 152-153 read `constexpr bool group_heads_ok(size_t g) noexcept {` / `  return g == GROUP_HEADS_4 || g == GROUP_HEADS_16;`, and `g` appears only on those two lines in the two AMX files.

judged.title: check_qk and check_pv are new 50- and 80-line helpers with no comment at their declaration; only the TEST_CASE names 150 lines below say what they check.
judged.body: Wade-code-review check 21 (explanation at the declaration). The PR moves the bodies of two TEST_CASEs into templated helpers. At HEAD `template <size_t group_heads>` / `void check_qk() {` [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:165-166] is preceded by a blank line, and the comment above it (:158-162) describes the sentinel constant, not the helper. `void check_pv() {` [:220] likewise has a blank line above it. Both are absent at BASE (the BASE TEST_CASEs held the bodies inline). The third helper, `check_q_pack` [:131], does carry its contract comment (:125-130), so the file's own pattern is one comment per helper. A reader of the helpers alone learns what they assert only from the TEST_CASE labels at :315 ("AMX QK does not digress from the AVX dotter") and :328 ("AMX PV stays inside the AVX weight-rounding envelope"). judged.title: `inline` on store_transposed_rows changes nothing: it is a function template inside an anonymous namespace.
judged.body: Wade-code-review check 22 (redundant specifier), his 'a bit pedantic but' form (2976643305). HEAD line 170 reads `inline void store_transposed_rows(` under `template <int lane>` [:169], inside the `namespace {` opened at :148 and closed at :185. A function template is already exempt from the one-definition rule, and the anonymous namespace already gives it internal linkage, so deleting `inline` changes no linkage, no type and no build. The PR body's object compare shows the 4-head QK kernel instruction-identical to main, so the specifier did not decide inlining either. fwiw only; no action needed.
judged.rule: Wade check 22 (redundant statement, member, branch, specifier or scope)
judged.evidence:
148: namespace {
169: template <int lane>
170: inline void store_transposed_rows(
185: }  // namespace
corrections: One wording nit before posting: the object compare shows that the function WAS inlined (the 4-head kernel is instruction-identical to main, where the store was written in place), but by itself it does not show that the `inline` specifier played no part in that decision. The stronger argument is structural: each instantiation `store_transposed_rows<0..3>` has a single call site [amx_attn.cpp:255, :257-259] inside an internal-linkage kernel, and clang at -O3 inlines such called-once internal functions regardless of the specifier. Suggest replacing "so the specifier did not decide inlining either" with "and each instantiation has a single call site [:255, :257-259], which clang at -O3 inlines regardless of the specifier".

Minor wording: "A function template is already exempt from the one-definition rule" is loose. The precise statement is that the one-definition rule already allows a function template to be defined in every translation unit, the same allowance `inline` grants a plain function; and the anonymous namespace makes the point moot by giving the template internal linkage. Optionally add that `detect_and_request` at HEAD line 86, the file's other anonymous-namespace function, carries no `inline`, so dropping it also matches the file's own idiom.

Replace "The PR body's object compare shows the 4-head QK kernel instruction-identical to main, so the specifier did not decide inlining either." with: "The specifier is not needed for inlining either: the body is a four-iteration shuffle loop, which -O3 inlines with or without the hint, and the PR body's object compare shows it folded into qk_rowmajor_128x4 (205 instructions, identical to main). The rest of the file agrees: detect_and_request() at :56 in the first anonymous namespace carries no inline, and :170 is the only inline function in amx_attn.cpp."

judged.title: The QK store branch keys on group_heads == 16 and silently treats every other size as 4 heads; nothing names that assumption.
judged.body: Check 27 (silent fallback where an assert belongs). The transposing store always runs lane 0 and adds lanes 1..3 only under one equality test: `store_transposed_rows<0>(u, s_block, s_stride_floats);` (src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:255) and `if constexpr (group_heads == GROUP_HEADS_16) {` (:256). The two other kernels are generic on the parameter: the pack loop is `for (size_t q_head = 0; q_head < group_heads; q_head++) {` (:138) and the P loop is `for (size_t q = 0; q < group_heads; q++) {` (:285). So only the QK store encodes "not 16 means 4". Today a bug-free caller cannot reach the implicit else with anything but 4: `requires(group_heads_ok(group_heads))` (:192) and `group_heads_ok` (h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:152-154) allow 4 and 16 only. If a third size were added to `group_heads_ok` (issue #5021 asks that a future shape be a minimal change), all three kernels would compile, pack and PV would serve the new size, and the QK kernel would write rows 0..3 of `s` only. The PV kernel would then read stale rows of `s_pages` for the other heads, and nothing would report it. Should the branch state its assumption so a third size fails to compile at this line? One form: `} else { static_assert(group_heads == GROUP_HEADS_4, "lane 0 stores rows 0..3, the 4-head case"); }`. Another: run lanes `< group_heads / ROWS_PER_LANE_4`. Nit, not blocking: unreachable at HEAD.
judged.rule: Wade-code-review check 27 (silent fallback where an assert belongs)
corrections: Replace "nothing names that assumption" with "only the comment at lines 247-250 names that assumption; nothing enforces it at compile time". The comment above the loop already says lanes 1..3 run only when group_heads is 16.

The finding should not be posted. If kept as a pure question, drop "nothing names that assumption" (the comment at amx_attn.cpp:227-230 and the requires clause at :192 name it) and drop the check 27 attribution, since the rule covers runtime guards a caller can reach, not a compile-time branch under a requires clause that admits exactly 4 and 16.

Replace "nothing names that assumption" / "So only the QK store encodes 'not 16 means 4'" with: the comment at src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:237-240 does name it in prose ("lanes 1..3 (rows 4..15) only when group_heads is 16"), but no compile-time check enforces it, so a third size added to group_heads_ok would compile and write rows 0..3 of s only. Keep the first fix form (else-branch static_assert); drop or demote the second form, since `lane` must stay a template argument (the shuffle selectors are immediates, :160-163), so a runtime lane loop would need an index-sequence helper. Note the static_assert message should be short enough for clang-format's 90 columns at 6-space indent (e.g. "lane 0 covers the 4-head case only"), or clang-format will wrap the string onto its own line, which is also acceptable.
refutations: Scope (a) holds: the `if constexpr (group_heads == GROUP_HEADS_16)` branch at src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:256 is new in this diff (BASE had one unconditional 0x88 store sequence at its lines 210-213). The finding fails on (b) and (c). (b) Check 27 reads: "Can a bug-free caller reach this? If not, why not assert, naming the value?" (SKILL.md:333-349). That assert already exists at compile time: `requires(group_heads_ok(group_heads))` on the kernel (amx_attn.cpp:192) and `group_heads_ok` returning `g == GROUP_HEADS_4 || g == GROUP_HEADS_16` (amx_attn_iface.hpp:152-154), with the comment "that file instantiates it for exactly this set" (iface:149-151). Any other group_heads fails to compile at :192 before the implicit else is ever instantiated. The title's claim "nothing names that assumption" is wrong: the comment at amx_attn.cpp:227-230 states "the store helper emits stages 3 and 4 for lane 0 (rows 0..3) always and for lanes 1..3 (rows 4..15) only when group_heads is 16", and :161-162 says "Lane 0 = (0x88, 0x88) is the one store sequence the 4-head kernel emits". Check 27's trigger list is runtime guards (clamp, silent exit, spin, sentinel) reachable by a caller; a compile-time branch under a requires clause that admits exactly two values, with no reachable third case, is not a silent fallback under that rule. (c) The only way to reach the implicit else is to edit `group_heads_ok` to add a third size; the finder itself ties that to "a future shape be a minimal change", which the PR body (pr-body.md:123) defers to issue #5021 and the task instructions exclude. The finder also concedes "unreachable at HEAD". The suggested static_assert would duplicate the requires clause one function above it.

judged.title: The 16-head QK and PV kernel sections never execute on the lane that gates this PR, and the only run that executed them is the author's local run.
judged.body:
Wade-code-review check 3A (a test must run, reach its assertion and observe the defect). Words used here: a lane is one CI workflow file with its trigger block and configure line. The gating lane is the workflow whose jobs `gh pr checks 5015 --required` lists.

Facts at HEAD 5061623a34:

1. Compiles on the lane: no. The required checks come from gcp-nix.yml (trigger `pull_request`, gcp-nix.yml:13). Its Build Tron job builds with `nix build "$recipe^testRuntime,benchmarkRuntime"` (gcp-nix.yml:501) from nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix, whose cmake_args list (:79-100) carries no `-DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH`. CMakeLists.txt:46 defaults the option OFF. So on the gating lane t_amx_numerics.cpp compiles only the `#else` stub at :342-346 (`SUCCEED("build without TRON_AMX_DISPATCH - nothing to test")`), and t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp only its stub at :318-321. The GCP Nix run at HEAD (run 39064711603, Test host job 117495894283 on runner andoria-09-0) prints `passed t_amx_numerics inst 0,8 0.5s` and `passed t_amx_dispatch_dtype 0.5s`: those are the stubs.
2. Selected: yes, t/CMakeLists.txt:619 and :622 register both binaries with `LABELS fake`, and the job runs `bin/slice run --filter=host`.
3. Reachable on the runner: the only lane that passes `-DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON` is cmake-single-platform.yml:355. That workflow has no `push` or `pull_request` trigger (its `on:` block is `workflow_dispatch` and `workflow_call`, :2-8). It runs from publish-deb.yml:68 on tag pushes, feature-branch publishes and the nightly schedule. Its test-host job uses `runs-on: [self-hosted, fpga, test, avx512]` (:381), which matches the andoria runners (Genoa, no AMX, README.ci.md:447-449) as well as the delphi runners. On an andoria runner the two kernel cases exit at :316-319 and :330-333 with a WARN, and the slice summary still says passed.
4. Log: the only execution of the sections `16 heads: all 16 rows match the dotter` (:323-325) and `16 heads` for PV (:337-339), and of the row-bound check at :213, is the author's local run on delphi-3bda (PR body, Verification, lines 46-53).

So if the 16-head transposing store were wrong (for example the two selectors at src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:174-175 swapped), every required check at HEAD stays green. The PR relies on the body's local run. The lane property is pre-existing (PR 4557 had the same gap), so this is a non-blocking question in Wade's register, not a blocker.

Ask, two repairs, either one answers it: (a) add one sentence to the body's `Builds and tests` section saying that the required checks at HEAD compile the AMX cases out and that the delphi-3bda run is the execution of the 16-head sections; (b) replace the `WARN(...); return;` at :317-318 and :331-332 with Catch2's `SKIP("AMX unavailable on this host")` (Catch2 3.3 and later mark the case skipped instead of passed), so that a kernel-lane run that lands on andoria reports a skip rather than `passed`. A runner route (`intel` label on the test-host job) would make the kernel cases execute in every run, but that is a CI-configuration change outside this PR.
judged.rule: Wade-code-review check 3A (gated or blind test); AGENTS.md:22-24 "Every committed test must run in CI. Before committing it, verify that a required CI suite collects and executes it; local execution and the test file's presence are not sufficient."
corrections: Minor: the quoted CI log line for the dtype test reads `passed t_amx_dispatch_dtype inst 2,8 0.5s` (the finding omits `inst 2,8`); no change to the claim. Optionally add that Catch2 is pinned at v3.7.1 [cmake/versions.cmake:26] and SKIP() is already used in t/t_disk_cache.cpp:182, which shows repair (b) needs no dependency change.

Remedy (b) overstates what SKIP changes. Catch2 is v3.7.1 (cmake/versions.cmake:26), so SKIP exists, but t_amx_numerics keeps two non-gated cases (the static checks and the Q packer case), so the binary still exits 0 and slice's status line (bin/slice:1208 status_for_returncode maps only return codes) would still print `passed t_amx_numerics`. SKIP would show the two cases as skipped only in Catch2's own summary inside the per-test log. Reword to: "so that Catch2's own summary for a kernel-lane run on andoria lists the two kernel cases as skipped instead of passed; slice's per-binary line stays `passed` because the two non-gated cases keep the exit code at 0."

Narrow the claim made for repair (b). bin/slice decides pass/skip by exit code only (bin/slice:123 `SKIP_RETURN_CODE_LABEL_RE`, :1181 `skip_return_codes_for`); with two of the four cases still running, a Catch2 SKIP leaves the exit code at 0, so the slice summary line still says "passed t_amx_numerics". What (b) changes is Catch2's own summary, which then prints the two cases as skipped instead of passed. Suggested wording: "so that Catch2's summary on a kernel-lane run that lands on andoria counts the two cases as skipped instead of passed (the slice line still says passed, since slice reads only the exit code)". Also note that with (b) the body's AMX-off row ("2 sections skipped with 'AMX unavailable on this host'") becomes "2 test cases skipped", and `return;` after SKIP is redundant (SKIP ends the test case).

judged.title: The second round of the 16-head dispatch section repeats what the 4-head section's second round already observes.
judged.body:
Wade-code-review check 4 (same experiment run twice). The new section at :299-303 calls `exercise_page<host_bf16, GROUP_HEADS_16>(page_size, /*repeat=*/true)`. Its round 0 is distinct from the 4-head section: it observes `probe.pack_group_heads == 16`, `probe.qk_group_heads == 16` and `probe.pv_group_heads == 16` (:202-204) and the 16 x 128 packed values with a per-head offset (:145-148, :237). A call site that hard-coded `GROUP_HEADS_4` instead of `geometry.kv_mul()` at self_attention.hpp:1696, :1763 or :1791 would fail here and nowhere else. That round earns its place.

Round 1 does not. What round 1 observes is that a second `apply_page_range` call packs again (:177-186). The state it probes is the per-call bitset `amx_packed` (self_attention.hpp:1549), which does not depend on the group size. The 4-head section at :292-295 already observes it. Round 1 also writes `expected[i] = -2.0f - (i % 8) * 0.5f` (:181), a pattern without a per-head offset, so it observes less about the pack than round 0 did. No break fails the 16-head round 1 and passes both the 4-head round 1 and the 16-head round 0.

Cost: about 2,100 extra REQUIREs per run (16 x 128 value compares plus the counters), well under a second. So this is a nit, not a blocker. AGENTS.md:42-43 rules out coverage that duplicates "without protecting a distinct behavior".

Proposed edit: `exercise_page<host_bf16, amx_attn_h128g4::GROUP_HEADS_16>(page_size);` and drop the clause `; a second call with new queries packs again` from the section name at :299-300 and from the file header line :17-18.

judged.title: The skip message still says "QK precision check skipped", but the case now also skips the row-bound check that the PR added.
judged.body:
Wade-code-review check 5 (test name, tags and result print agree with assertions). The TEST_CASE at :315 gained a second contract in this PR: rows `group_heads..15` of `s` stay untouched (the sentinel loop at :210-214, explained at :158-162). That is a layout contract (the kernel writes only `group_heads` rows, so `s` needs only `group_heads` rows), not a precision check. The WARN at :317 names only the precision check, so a reader of a skipped run on a host without AMX does not learn that the row-bound check was skipped too. Same at :331 for PV, where the text is accurate (PV has no new contract), so only :317 needs the edit.

Suggestion:
```suggestion
    WARN("AMX unavailable on this host - QK dotter and row-bound checks skipped");
```
If repair (b) of the check 3A finding is taken (a Catch2 `SKIP`), put the same text there.
judged.rule: Wade-code-review check 5 (test label and result print match the assertions)
refutations: Scope (a) holds: HEAD :317 is byte-identical to BASE :150 (`WARN("AMX unavailable on this host - QK precision check skipped");`), but the diff added the sentinel assertions at HEAD :210-214 inside the same case and the line sits in the diff range [300,344], so the diff did change the context. The finding fails on rule (b). Wade check 5 (SKILL.md :573-587) asks "does the label describe the passing state and match its siblings?", triggers on (A) a name that keeps its verb while the body's assertion flips, (B) tags that break the file convention, (C) an unguarded counter print before a zero REQUIRE, and its finding shape is "the section is still named '<name>', but it now asserts that <opposite state>". The WARN at :317 is none of these: it is a skip notice, not a label of the passing state, it states nothing false (the precision check is skipped), it does not contradict any assertion, and it follows its sibling exactly (:331 `WARN("AMX unavailable on this host - PV precision check skipped");`). The labels check 5 does govern already carry the new contract: TEST_CASE :315 "AMX QK does not digress from the AVX dotter" and SECTION :320 "4 heads: rows 0..3 match the dotter, rows 4..15 untouched", which Catch2 prints next to the WARN on a skipped run. Wade's three precedents (tron#1666, #2078, #4557) are a contradicting section name, a tag convention break and an unguarded counter print; none is an incomplete skip message. The PR body (pr-body.md :53) also presents the skip text as "2 sections skipped with 'AMX unavailable on this host' (the precision checks need the kernel)", so the wording is consistent with what the author describes. The suggested text is harmless, but it is incompleteness, not a check-5 mismatch, and the skill says a finding the rule does not support is dropped.

The consequence is hypothetical. The WARN at t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:317 is followed by `return;` at :318 before any SECTION runs, so it is a whole-case skip marker, not a per-assertion label. Catch2 prints a WARN under the test case name (:315 "AMX QK does not digress from the AVX dotter"), and the row-bound contract is already visible in the section name at :320 ("4 heads: rows 0..3 match the dotter, rows 4..15 untouched"). A reader of a skipped run cannot conclude that only part of the case ran, because nothing in the case runs after :318. The PR body (pr-body.md line 53) reads the message the same way: "2 sections skipped with 'AMX unavailable on this host'". The sentinel loop at :210-214 is new in the diff, but it is an assertion inside check_qk, the same as the dotter compare; "QK precision check" at :317 names the case, mirroring "PV precision check" at :331. Enumerating assertions in one skip message and not the other would make the two messages asymmetric and would drift again on the next assertion added. The proposed fix compiles and fits 90 columns, but it does not remove any real reading cost, so it is not worth a reviewer comment even at nit severity. If the separate check-3A finding (Catch2 SKIP) is taken, the message gets rewritten there anyway.

judged.title: The Verification section names raw-result files that a GitHub reader cannot open.
judged.body: Check 9 (passages a later reader cannot use: machine paths and log names in a Verification section). Line 46 ends 'Raw results: rt-results.txt, attn-stats-compare.md, tests.txt and local-obj-compare/ (result set glimmer-20261016)'; line 85 says '(the rows are in rt-results.txt)'; line 87 cites '(attn-stats-compare.md)'; line 94 says 'summary.md records the harness settings'; line 104 says 'Raw results: perf.json per pass (every request) and summary.md (result set glimci-20261017)'. None of these files is in the repository at HEAD (`git ls-tree -r HEAD` has no rt-results.txt, attn-stats-compare.md, tests.txt, local-obj-compare or glimci-20261017), and none is attached to the PR. So the references cost the reader a lookup that ends nowhere, and the prefill rows the body summarises at line 85 ('by 0.6 to 8.7 % with FPGA attention, by 1.3 to 14.8 % with CPU attention') have no row in the body at all. Please either attach the files to the PR (or link a notebook page) or drop the names, and put the prefill rows into a table in the body like the decode table at lines 73-83. Keep the commit id, the dates and the outcome clauses.
judged.rule: Wade check 9 (PR-body passages a GitHub reader cannot use)
judged.evidence:
pr-body.md:46: '... Raw results: rt-results.txt, attn-stats-compare.md, tests.txt and local-obj-compare/ (result set glimmer-20261016).'
pr-body.md:85: 'Prefill time shortens in every cell: ... (the rows are in rt-results.txt).'
pr-body.md:104: 'Raw results: perf.json per pass (every request) and summary.md (result set glimci-20261017).'
corrections: Narrow the ask to what check 9 supports. The rule's finding shape is "<the names> can go. Keep the rc/outcome clause and one result row per test and tree with the commit id and date." It does not ask the author to attach files or to add a prefill table. Replace the last two sentences of the comment with: "Please drop the file names (or replace each with a link a GitHub reader can open), and keep the commit id, the dates and the outcome clauses." The sentence about the prefill rows having no table at line 85 is a separate suggestion, not a check-9 item: either drop it or mark it as optional ("if you want the prefill numbers to be checkable without the raw file, a table like the decode one at lines 73-83 would do it"). Also soften the severity to nit; check 9's precedent is minor and never blocking.
refutations:
The finding does not hold under the rule it cites, and its fix goes against the project's own PR-body convention.

1. Check 9 does not fire on these lines by its own procedure. The check's bins are "machine paths and log names (delete)" and its grep is `/var/tmp/|/tmp/|/home/|*.log|clock times|reconciliations` (Wade-code-review procedures.md "Check 9", step 2). Running that grep on pr-body.md returns no hit (exit 1). pr-body.md:46 ("Raw results: rt-results.txt, attn-stats-compare.md, tests.txt and local-obj-compare/ (result set glimmer-20261016)"), :85 ("the rows are in rt-results.txt") and :104 ("Raw results: perf.json per pass ... summary.md (result set glimci-20261017)") carry bare result-set names, no host, no path, no .log. Check 9 also lists "a commit id plus a date that identifies the binary a result came from" and "the pass or fail outcome and the counts at the head" under "Do not fire on"; line 46 carries exactly those (head 5061623a34, base 6198824246, 2026-10-16/17) next to the file names.

2. Naming the result file is what the project's PR-description skill tells the author to do, not a defect. SKILL.md line 30: "When an issue or a result record holds a fact, the body names it and does not repeat it." Line 78: keep out "setup lists that a script or result file already records (name the file instead)". Line 106 (cut order when the body is long): "Verification tables: keep the rows the decision rests on, and name the result file for the rest." The body is at 2,018 words by the skill's own count (`awk '/^## Words used here/{skip=1; next} /^## /{skip=0} !skip' pr-body.md | wc -w`), already at the 2,000-word limit. The finding's fix (a second 9-row prefill table) adds roughly 100 words and reverses the cut the skill prescribes. The decision rows (decode TPS per cell, lines 73-83; kv_mul-4 llama cell, line 83; CI arm table, lines 106-111) are all in the body.

3. The stated consequence is minor. The reader has the commit id, the date, the headline prefill range (line 3 and line 85), the band rule (line 71) and the outcome clause ("every difference ... is beyond its band", line 85). The lookup costs nothing a decision depends on; the token-identity and kill-switch-vs-no-AMX-build gaps are already declared as Open items (lines 117-119). "Attach the files to the PR" is not a convention this repository uses (the Wade record and the PR-description skill both point to result records by name).

If a reviewer still wants the prefill claim checkable from the body, the smaller ask is two extra columns (prefill time AMX off / AMX on) on the existing decode table at lines 73-83, which keeps the word count near the limit. That is a nit, not a should-fix, and it is not a check 9 finding.

judged.title: The Short version claims the kv_mul-4 kernels 'emit the same instructions as on main', wider than the object compare shows for the PV kernel.
judged.body: Check 6 (a claim wider than the code or the evidence). Line 3 says 'the kv_mul-4 kernels emit the same instructions as on main'. The Verification table at line 63 says of weights_times_v_128x4: 'differs only in how the thread-local scratch is addressed (main local-dynamic, branch general-dynamic, the register and offset differences follow from it). The linker rewrites both to the same code'. So of the three kernels, two objects are identical and one is not; the headline sentence covers all three. The clause that rescues it, 'The linker rewrites both to the same code', has no measurement behind it in the body: line 46 says the compare was done 'at -O3 on amx_attn.cpp ... outside the build system', i.e. on the object files, before linking. Also, general-dynamic-to-local-exec and local-dynamic-to-local-exec relaxations produce equivalent but not byte-identical sequences, so 'the same code' would need a linked-binary compare to stand. The cause is the template's static local at src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:284 ('alignas(64) thread_local uint16_t P[TILE_ROWS_16][PAGE_TOKENS_64] = {};'), which has vague linkage once the function is a template. Narrow the text or widen the evidence: 'the kv_mul-4 pack and QK kernels are instruction-identical to main; the PV kernel differs only in the thread-local addressing of its P scratch' in the Short version, and either drop 'The linker rewrites both to the same code' or add the compare of the linked runtron symbols that supports it.
judged.rule: Wade check 6 (claim wider than the code)
judged.evidence:
pr-body.md:3: '... and the kv_mul-4 kernels emit the same instructions as on main.'
pr-body.md:63: '| weights_times_v_128x4 | 122 | 122 | 207 | differs only in how the thread-local scratch is addressed (main local-dynamic, branch general-dynamic, the register and offset differences follow from it). The linker rewrites both to the same code |'
src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:284: '  alignas(64) thread_local uint16_t P[TILE_ROWS_16][PAGE_TOKENS_64] = {};'
corrections: Strengthen one point: the PV listings differ not only in the TLS access model but also in register allocation across the tile loop (main %rsi/%rcx/%rdx/%rax, branch %rdi/%rax/%rsi/%rcx, lines 44-115 of the diff of main-weights_times_v_128x4.s vs r2-4-weights_times_v_128x4.s). A linker rewrites relocations, not register choices, so "The linker rewrites both to the same code" is wrong for those lines, not merely unmeasured. The suggested rewrite should therefore say the PV kernel "differs in the thread-local addressing of its P scratch and in register allocation; behaviour is the same" and drop the linker clause (or replace it with a linked-binary compare if one is made). Also note that the body itself already states the PV difference at line 42 ("PV differs only in the thread-local access model"), so the Short version contradicts the body's own review guide.

If posted at all, post it as a nit under PR-description precision, not as Wade check 6 should-fix. Keep the facts (they hold): pack and QK objects identical; PV object differs in the thread-local access model (main local-dynamic, branch general-dynamic, per the stored .s files) plus register renames; no linked-binary compare in result set glimmer-20261016. Suggested text change: line 3 'the kv_mul-4 pack and QK kernels are instruction-identical to main; the PV kernel differs only in how its thread-local P scratch is addressed'; line 63 either drop 'The linker rewrites both to the same code' or replace it with 'Both relax to local-exec TLS at link time (not compared on the linked runtron)'.

Keep the problem; shorten the fix. The user's convention keeps the Short version free of implementation detail (PR 4424 rule: details go in the body sections), so do not add the thread-local clause to line 3. Narrow line 3 instead by dropping the PV kernel from the headline: "and the kv_mul-4 pack and QK kernels emit the same instructions as on main" (the PV difference is already stated at lines 42 and 63). At line 63 replace "The linker rewrites both to the same code" with either nothing or "Both relax to local-exec when linked into the executable (tron is a static library); equivalent, not compared byte for byte on the linked runtron". The comment should also note that line 42 already narrows the claim, so the ask is consistency between line 3 and lines 42/63, not a hidden difference.
refutations:
Refuted on the rule lens (b), with the facts partly conceded.

(a) Scope: the sentence is new PR-body text for this head, so it is in scope. The code it rests on is real: src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:284 'alignas(64) thread_local uint16_t P[TILE_ROWS_16][PAGE_TOKENS_64] = {};' now sits inside 'template <size_t group_heads>' (amx_attn.cpp:264-266), while at BASE the same line (BASE amx_attn.cpp:232) was in a non-template function. The stored compare (exec/results/glimmer-20261016/local-obj-compare/main-weights_times_v_128x4.s vs r2-4-weights_times_v_128x4.s) confirms the body row: main emits the local-dynamic pair 'lea 0x0(%rip),%rdi / call', the branch the general-dynamic pair 'data16 lea 0x0(%rip),%rdi / data16 data16 rex.W call', followed by offset and register renames; pack and QK objects diff clean. No linked-binary compare exists in that result set, so 'The linker rewrites both to the same code' is indeed unmeasured.

(b) Rule: Wade check 6 (SKILL.md:631-646) triggers only on 'a body, commit, Note or doc sentence claiming (a) a compile-time type guarantee, (b) a timer or counter's scope, (c) a [0]-read container's count ..., or (d) a twice-stated default'. A summary of an object-code compare is none of the four subjects, and the check's finding shape ('`X` is only <timed | enforced> at <file:line>') does not fit it. The check also says 'Do not fire on: stated limitations', and the body states this limitation twice: pr-body.md:42 'the object compare in [Verification] (pack and QK identical, PV differs only in the thread-local access model)' and pr-body.md:63 (the full PV row). The Short version at line 3 is the summary those two lines qualify. The remaining substance (an unmeasured link-time sentence) is a measurement-method point, which the skill records as 'never more than a nit' (SKILL.md:854-866, 'Benchmark or measurement: 1 of 269 ... a wish'), not a should-fix.

(c) Body: the PV difference is answered at lines 42 and 63; the names are not involved.

So the finding is a plain-English/PR-description precision nit mislabelled as Wade check 6 at should-fix severity. If the author tightens the text anyway, the finder's proposed wording is accurate.

judged.title: No sentence says that the checks gating this PR compile the AMX code out; the green checks are not evidence for the kernels.
judged.body: Check 7 (CI claims name the lane, the trigger and the configure line). The body's 'Builds and tests' rows (lines 50-53) and line 46 describe the author's own build on delphi-3bda with '-DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON', which is a measurement statement and fine. What the body never says is what the PR's required checks compile. The gating lane is GCP Nix (gcp-nix.yml, on: push to main, pull_request, merge_group; `gh pr checks 5015 --required` lists its Build Tron, Test host, Test FPGA, Test jobs). Its build recipe nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix:79-101 passes no TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, and CMakeLists.txt:46 defaults the option OFF. So on that lane src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp is not compiled, every self_attention.hpp hunk of this PR sits under `#ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` (h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:276, :1528, :1681) and is excluded, and the two AMX test binaries run their placeholder cases: t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:344 'AMX numerics tests skipped (dispatch not compiled)' and t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:319 'AMX dispatch dtype test skipped (dispatch not compiled)'. The only workflow that sets the option is cmake-single-platform.yml:355 ('-DTRON_REQUIRE_ALL_MODEL_TESTS=ON -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON', runs-on [self-hosted, fpga, test, avx512], Test Host at :468), and it has only workflow_dispatch and workflow_call triggers (cmake-single-platform.yml:5-12); publish-deb.yml:68 calls it under the gate at :64-67, `startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/') || feature_branch == '1'`, where bin/ci/resolve-apt-channel.sh:25-28 sets feature_branch only for a refs/heads branch that is not main or release-*. So the scheduled nightly on main skips it too. Consequence: a reader who takes the 12 green required checks as execution of the 16-head kernels is wrong; the author's run at 5061623a34 on delphi-3bda is the only execution named anywhere. Please add one sentence under 'Builds and tests': the required checks (GCP Nix) build without TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, so the rows above are the only runs of the kernels. fwiw, body line 55 'CI runs it' (clang-format) is right: the GCP Nix Lint job (gcp-nix.yml:54, bin/ci/run-lint-checks.sh) builds the lint-toolchain check, which runs clang-format-19 (flake.nix:2322-2323).
judged.rule: Wade check 7 (CI claims name the lane, the trigger and the configure line)
judged.evidence:
pr-body.md:46: 'Every result below comes from head 5061623a34 ... built inside `nix develop` with clang 19.1.7, preset `native`, RelWithDebInfo, `-DBUILD_INGEST_MODELS=ON -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON`.'
.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml:355: '          -DTRON_REQUIRE_ALL_MODEL_TESTS=ON -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON'
.github/workflows/publish-deb.yml:64-68: 'if: >- !cancelled() && (startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/') || needs.resolve-channel.outputs.feature_branch == '1')  uses: ./.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml'
CMakeLists.txt:46: 'option(TRON_AMX_DISPATCH "Compile the AMX software-attention kernels and their dispatch ..." OFF)'
t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:344: 'TEST_CASE("AMX numerics tests skipped (dispatch not compiled)", "[amx_numerics]") {'
corrections: Drop or narrow the sentence "So the scheduled nightly on main skips it too" and the phrase "The only workflow that sets the option is cmake-single-platform.yml:355". The nightly publish-deb run (schedule cron at publish-deb.yml:21-22) builds the package with `make deb` (publish-deb.yml:111), which configures with `cmake --preset deb` (GNUmakefile:510), and the deb preset sets "TRON_AMX_DISPATCH": "ON" (CMakePresets.json:68). So the nightly skips only the cmake-single-platform host-test lane; its deb contains the AMX kernels, and the PR body's "Performance at the CI configuration" section (lines 92-113) already measures that deb. The correct statement is: the required checks on this PR (GCP Nix) build without TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, so the AMX host tests of this PR run nowhere in CI; the kernels themselves reach CI only through the nightly deb perf phase after merge.

1. 'The only workflow that sets the option is cmake-single-platform.yml:355' is incomplete. The `deb` preset also sets it: CMakePresets.json:68 `"TRON_AMX_DISPATCH": "ON"`, and publish-deb.yml's build job produces gen-deb/tron_*_amd64.deb from that preset (publish-deb.yml:122) on its nightly schedule (publish-deb.yml:20-21). So the nightly deb on main does compile the kernels (which is why body line 98 can say the base deb's gate refuses Glimmer); what it never does for a PR is run the AMX test binaries, and no PR check builds a deb. Replace the sentence with: 'Outside the PR checks, the option is set only by cmake-single-platform.yml:355 (workflow_dispatch/workflow_call) and by the deb preset (CMakePresets.json:68) that the nightly publish-deb build on main uses.' 2. The proposed body sentence 'the rows above are the only runs of the kernels' is too narrow: the performance cells and the CI-configuration arms below are kernel runs too. Suggest instead, under 'Builds and tests': 'The PR's required checks (GCP Nix) build without TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, so they compile none of the AMX code and run the placeholder test cases. Every run of the kernels in this section is the author's run on delphi-3bda.' 3. Anchor the comment at body line 55 ('CI runs it'), the body's only CI sentence, not line 46, which the finder itself calls a correct measurement statement.
refutations:
Refuted on the rule (lens b) and on scope (lens a).

Rule: Wade check 7 fires only on an existing sentence. Its trigger reads "a sentence in the PR body ... has a CI subject ... it asserts a setting or coverage ... it is not about a build the author made (a named tree, machine or runtron arm is a measurement statement)" [~/.claude/skills/Wade-code-review/SKILL.md:648-653], and its finding shape opens with "'<quoted sentence>' names no lane" [SKILL.md:670]. The finder anchors on pr-body.md:46 ("Every result below comes from head 5061623a34 ... on delphi-3bda ... -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON") and itself says that line "is a measurement statement and fine". The finding then asks for a sentence that does not exist to be added. Check 7 verifies CI claims; it does not require a CI-coverage disclaimer. The only CI-subject sentences in the body are line 55 ("CI runs it", clang-format), which the finder confirms as correct and does not report, and lines 94/108 (the nightly perf phase shape and GitHub Actions run 38999609242), which assert no build setting and are not targeted. No sentence in the body claims the required checks executed the kernels, so the "reader who takes the 12 green required checks as execution of the 16-head kernels" is not a claim the body makes.

Scope: the gating facts the finder relies on are unchanged from BASE. CMakeLists.txt:46 defaults TRON_AMX_DISPATCH OFF at HEAD and at BASE 6198824246 (git show BASE:CMakeLists.txt line 46 identical). The `#ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` guards in h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp sit at 254, 276, 477, 1528, 1630, 1681 at HEAD and at the same lines at BASE. The placeholder cases exist at BASE too (BASE t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:284 and BASE t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:285, same TEST_CASE strings as HEAD :344 and :319). The nearest check that mentions a flag-off lane compiling a case out is 3A step 3 [SKILL.md:486], a test check with its own finding shape, and its do-not-fire list excludes exits present at BASE [SKILL.md:508]. The finder's workflow citations (cmake-single-platform.yml:355, publish-deb.yml:64-68, gcp-nix.yml on: push/pull_request/merge_group) are accurate, but they establish a pre-existing CI layout, not a defect this PR introduces or a claim its body makes.

judged.title: 'A caller with any other size fails to link' names the wrong mechanism: the requires clause rejects it at compile time.
judged.body: Check 6 (which code line reaches what the sentence says). Line 35 says 'the explicit instantiations at the end of the file: the same two sizes. A caller with any other size fails to link.' Each kernel declaration carries `requires(group_heads_ok(group_heads))` (h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:202-203, :242-243, :256-257), and group_heads_ok at :152-154 is true for 4 and 16 only. A call such as `pack_q_group_128x4<8>(...)` therefore has no viable candidate and fails to compile ('no matching function'); it never reaches the linker. The explicit instantiation list at src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:333-354 is the link-time backstop that would matter only if the constraint were dropped. The sentence as written sends a reviewer to look for a link error that cannot happen. Replace with: 'A caller with any other size fails to compile (the requires clause); without that clause it would fail to link, because only these two sizes are instantiated.'
judged.rule: Wade check 6 (claim wider than the code)
judged.evidence:
pr-body.md:35: '- `src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp`, the explicit instantiations at the end of the file: the same two sizes. A caller with any other size fails to link. A model with any other kv_mul is refused by the gate.'
h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:202-204: 'template <size_t group_heads>\n  requires(group_heads_ok(group_heads))\nvoid pack_q_group_128x4(const bf16* q_group, bf16* packed) noexcept;'
corrections: None to the substance. One wording note for the proposed replacement: say 'fails to compile (the requires clause on each kernel, amx_attn_iface.hpp:203/243/257)' so the reader can find the three lines; the rest of the suggested sentence is accurate.

None needed. Optional precision for the comment: the compiler diagnostic is 'no matching function ... constraints not satisfied' (unsatisfied requires clause), and the instantiation list at amx_attn.cpp:334-354 (HEAD lines; the finding's 333-354 range starts on a blank line) is a link-time backstop only if the constraint were removed.

Suggested shorter replacement for the sentence: "A caller with any other size fails to compile: the requires clause has no match. The instantiation list is the link-time backstop and must stay equal to group_heads_ok."

judged.title: The QK object-compare row (205 vs 208 listing lines) cannot hold the '40 vshuf shuffles in the 16-head kernel only' it reports.
judged.body: Check 8 (result rows match the head they describe). Line 62 reads '| qk_rowmajor_128x4 | 205 | 205 | 208 | identical (16 `tdpbf16ps` tile multiplies in each, and 40 `vshuf` shuffles in the 16-head kernel only) |'. If a listing line is one instruction (line 57 says 'lines of each disassembly listing, one of which is the label line'), the 16-head QK kernel is 3 instructions longer than the 4-head one. At HEAD the 16-head instantiation adds three store_transposed_rows calls per r iteration (src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:256-260), each with 4 stores and 12 shuffles before any common-subexpression sharing (:177-182); even with maximal sharing of the stage-3 shuffles that is at least 12 stores plus 20 shuffles per r iteration more than the 4-head kernel. Forty extra shuffles do not fit in three extra lines, so one of the two numbers in the row describes something other than what the column header says. The row is the evidence behind 'Is the kv_mul-4 path unchanged?' (line 42), so it should be self-consistent. Could you restate what the three count columns measure (whole-symbol instruction count, or something filtered), or correct the 208? Insufficient data on my side: I could not rebuild the objects in this session, so this is a consistency question, not a measured refutation.
judged.rule: Wade check 8 (result rows cite the reviewed head)
refutations: The row is literally true and self-consistent. The raw listings the PR body cites (local-obj-compare/, result set glimmer-20261016) exist at /home/jhan/workspace/intel-AMX/exec/results/glimmer-20261016/local-obj-compare/. wc -l gives main-qk_rowmajor_128x4.s 205, r2-4-qk_rowmajor_128x4.s 205, r2-16-qk_rowmajor_128x4.s 208 lines (one label line each), and cmp shows main and the 4-head branch listing are byte-identical. grep -c gives tdpbf16ps = 16 in all three and vshuff64x2 = 40 in the 16-head listing, 0 in the other two. So all four numbers in line 62 match the column headers (whole-symbol disassembly line counts). The finder's premise that 16 heads must add at least 12 stores plus 20 shuffles per r iteration on top of the 4-head code assumes both kernels are compiled with the same loop shape. They are not: the 4-head listing is fully unrolled over the four r iterations (no cmp/jne, 32 vinsertf128 + 16 vinsertf64x4 + 16 vmovups = 4 iterations x the lane-0 store, which clang lowers to inserts rather than vshuff), while the 16-head listing keeps r as a runtime loop (1 cmp, 1 jne at listing line 204, 15 add) whose single body holds the 40 vshuff64x2 and 16 vmovupd stores for all four lanes. One rolled loop body with 40 shuffles comes out to about the same line count as four unrolled lane-0 bodies, hence 208 vs 205. Source lines src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:255-260 ('store_transposed_rows<0>(u, ...); if constexpr (group_heads == GROUP_HEADS_16) { store_transposed_rows<1>... <3> }') are the per-iteration source cost the finder counted, but the object counts in the row are the compiled result, which the saved listings reproduce exactly.

The row is a measured result from the reviewed head, and it is self-consistent. The raw listings the PR body names (line 46: "Raw results: rt-results.txt, attn-stats-compare.md, tests.txt and local-obj-compare/") exist at /home/jhan/workspace/intel-AMX/exec/results/glimmer-20261016/local-obj-compare/. `wc -l` on main-qk_rowmajor_128x4.s / r2-4-qk_rowmajor_128x4.s / r2-16-qk_rowmajor_128x4.s gives 205 / 205 / 208, `grep -c tdpbf16ps` gives 16 / 16 / 16, and `grep -c vshuf` gives 0 / 0 / 40. Every number in pr-body.md line 62 matches the listings, so the three count columns do measure what the header says (listing lines of the whole symbol).

The finder's premise ("3 more lines means the 16-head kernel is 3 instructions longer per r iteration, so 40 extra shuffles cannot fit") is wrong because static listing length is code size, not per-iteration instruction count. The 4-head listing is fully unrolled over the four r iterations (0 backward branches; 32 `vinsertf128` loads fold the lane-0 selection straight out of the stack tile store, so no shuffle is needed), while the 16-head listing keeps the r loop (one `cmp $0x13c0,%rsi; jne` back-edge, 0 `vinsertf128`, 40 `vshuff64x2` in one loop body). One rolled body with 40 shuffles is about the same size as four unrolled bodies with 32 inserts, which is why the totals are 205 and 208.

Lens (b): Wade check 8 ("Result rows, body sentences and the branch state match the reviewed head", ~/.claude/skills/Wade-code-review/SKILL.md:672-680) triggers on stale ids, commits after the body's last edit, conflicts, ported files. The row cites head 5061623a34 (pr-body.md line 46) and the raw files date 2026-10-16, the day of the head; no later commit is involved. An arithmetic plausibility doubt is not a check-8 trigger, and the finder itself states it is not a measured refutation.

Lens (c): the PR body already points to the raw listings (line 46), which answer the question.

The raw listings behind the row exist at /home/jhan/workspace/intel-AMX/exec/results/glimmer-20261016/local-obj-compare/ and resolve the question. wc -l gives exactly the row's numbers: main-qk_rowmajor_128x4.s 205, r2-4-qk_rowmajor_128x4.s 205, r2-16-qk_rowmajor_128x4.s 208, so the columns are whole-symbol listing lines as pr-body.md:57 says. The finding's inference (3 more lines cannot hold 40 more shuffles) assumes both kernels have the same loop structure. They do not. In the 4-head listing clang fully unrolls the r loop (0 jump instructions, 4 copies of the transpose) and lowers the lane-0-only stages 3/4 into a different instruction mix: 0 vshuf, 48 vinsertf128/vinsertf64x4, 32 vunpck, 48 vmovups/vmovaps. In the 16-head listing clang keeps the r loop (1 jump, one copy of the body): 40 vshuf, 32 vunpck, 8 vinsert, 32 vmov. Both have 16 tdpbf16ps. So '40 vshuf shuffles in the 16-head kernel only' is literally measured (grep -c vshuf = 40 vs 0), the 208 is the real line count, and the row is self-consistent. The HEAD code the finder cites (src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:256-260, the three extra store_transposed_rows calls) is correctly described by the row; the per-iteration cost estimate in the finding is not wrong, it just does not translate into listing lines because the 4-head kernel is unrolled 4x and the 16-head one is not. No correction to the PR body is needed; at most an optional clause ('the 4-head listing is unrolled, the 16-head keeps the r loop') could be added, which is not a defect.

judged.title: The review guide names the instruction 'vshufps'; the code uses _mm512_shuffle_f32x4, which assembles to vshuff32x4.
judged.body: Check 6 (does each identifier in a claim sentence match the code line). Line 28 says 'row `4*l + k` of `s` uses the `vshufps` selector `0x88` when bit 0 of `l` is 0 and `0xdd` when it is 1'. The helper at src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:178-181 calls `_mm512_shuffle_f32x4`, whose instruction is VSHUFF32X4 (128-bit lane shuffle); VSHUFPS is a different instruction (32-bit element shuffle within 128-bit lanes) and would not implement the lane selection the comment at :155-160 describes. A reviewer who greps the disassembly for vshufps to verify the claim finds nothing; line 62 already counts '`vshuf` shuffles', which matches vshuff32x4. Suggested text: 'uses the `_mm512_shuffle_f32x4` (vshuff32x4) selector `0x88` ...'. The selector arithmetic itself checks out: after the unpack stages at :241-252, 128-bit lane l of u[row_group][k] holds tile column 4*l + k, and 0x88 picks lanes {0,2} and 0xdd lanes {1,3} of each input, so lane bit 0 drives stage 3 and bit 1 drives stage 4, writing row 4*lane + k at :176-181.

judged.title: The per-head query offset in the dispatch test is explained in the commit message but not in the body's review guide.
judged.body: Check 10 (hunk-to-claim trace, test hunk). Lines 142-147 replace the BASE fill 'expected[i] = 1.0f + static_cast<float>(i % 4) * 0.25f' with one that adds 'static_cast<float>(i / head_size) * HEAD_OFFSET_STEP_0_0625', so every head carries a distinct value. The callee this guards, the pack fake at :257-264, is rewritten by the PR (it now copies group_heads * HEAD_SIZE_128 values and records group_heads), so the hunk is a regression guard, not an unrelated change. Commit 393dbc1759 says why ('The query fill gives every head its own offset so a head permutation cannot pass'), but the body's bullet at line 37 ('The `t_amx_dispatch_dtype` fakes ... record the group size of every pack, QK and PV call and require it to equal the model's') does not mention it, and a reviewer reading the diff from the body meets an unexplained fixture change. fwiw: one clause in line 37, 'and the query fill gives each head its own offset so a permuted or dropped head fails the value check at :235-238', closes it. The comment at :142-144 is right that 2.6875 is exact in bf16 (1 + 15/16 + 3/4 = 43/16, 7 significant bits).
judged.rule: Wade check 10 (hunk-to-claim trace: test hunk is a regression guard; body gap at most)
corrections: The parenthetical '1 + 15/16 + 3/4 = 43/16, 7 significant bits' overstates the bit count: 43 = 101011 in binary, so 2.6875 = 0x1.58p+1 has 6 significant bits (bf16 holds 8). Write '6 significant bits' or drop the count; the exactness claim itself is correct.

If the author still wants the clause, cite the value check as t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:234-238 (the "if (packs)" block starts at 234, the REQUIRE is at 237), and add it to the Verification bullet at pr-body.md:37 as: "The query fill gives each head its own offset (t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:142-147), so a pack that permutes or drops a head fails the value check at :234-238."
refutations: Scope (a) holds: the hunk is new in this diff (BASE t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:134 'expected[i] = 1.0f + static_cast<float>(i % 4) * 0.25f;' became HEAD :142-147). Rule (b) does not hold. Wade check 10 step 5 (SKILL.md:741): 'A candidate in the same function or TEST_CASE as a hunk that carries an identifier inherits that hunk's status.' The fill hunk sits inside exercise_page (HEAD :80-241). The same function carries the hunk at HEAD :201-204 ('REQUIRE(probe.pack_group_heads == (packs ? n_heads : 0));' and the qk/pv lines), whose added lines contain the PR identifier group_heads (backticked in pr-body.md:35, 0 hits at BASE by git grep, 81 at HEAD; the rule confirms identifiers with a plain grep -c, which matches pack_group_heads/qk_group_heads/pv_group_heads). So the fill hunk inherits MAIN-FEATURE status and is not a check-10 candidate; the check does not fire. Even without inheritance, the finding itself concedes the hunk is a regression guard for the rewritten pack fake (HEAD :255-264) and that the bf16 claim at :142-144 is correct, so there is no defect; what remains is a sentence-level wish for the body at pr-body.md:37, which the rule allows only in the shape 'the body never says <callee> keeps <contract>' for a candidate hunk, and this hunk is not one. Commit 393dbc1759 already states the reason ('The query fill gives every head its own offset so a head permutation cannot pass'). Not excluded by (c): the body does not describe the fill, and issue #5021 is unrelated.

The facts hold but the consequence does not. The finding's stated cost is that a reviewer reading the diff from the body "meets an unexplained fixture change". The hunk explains itself in place: t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:142-144 reads "Each head carries its own offset (i / head_size), so a pack that permutes or drops heads cannot pass; every value is exact in bf16. The offset step is 1/16: head 15 gives at most 2.6875, exact in bf16." That is the same sentence the finding wants added to the body, already at the lines a diff reader looks at. The hunk also traces to a body claim: pr-body.md:37 names the t_amx_dispatch_dtype fakes and the group-size requirement, and the fill is the fixture that makes the 16-head section's value check (t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:234-238, "if (packs) { ... REQUIRE(probe.q[i] == expected[i]); }") meaningful once the pack fake copies group_heads * HEAD_SIZE_128 values (:257-264). Wade check 10 flags hunks with no claim to trace to; this hunk has both a claim and an inline rationale, and the commit message repeats it (commits.txt:66-67). The proposed clause would be harmless (prose only, no compile, format or test effect, nothing the body says was avoided), but it restates a comment the reviewer reads in the same hunk. The body also does not enumerate fixture details for the other sections of this test (sentinel-level detail is given only for the t_amx_numerics QK case at pr-body.md:30), so the gap is not an inconsistency in the body's own level of detail. A fwiw PR comment asking for a body clause that duplicates the in-code comment is noise, not a review finding. Minor: the finding cites the value check at :235-238; the block starts at :234.

judged.title: `probe` has no non-template consumer at HEAD, so the gating Build Tron job now warns "variable 'probe' is not needed and will not be emitted".
judged.body: Check 14 (added symbol needs a consumer at HEAD) and check 16 (a change that ships a new diagnostic on the target branch). At BASE the three fakes were plain functions, so `probe` always had an emitted reader (BASE t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:236-253: `void pack_q_group_128x4(...) { ++probe.pack_calls; ...`). At HEAD every reader of `probe` sits inside a template: the fakes at :255-284 and `exercise_page` at :79-241. On the required check "Build Tron" (nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix, TRON_AMX_DISPATCH absent, default OFF) nothing instantiates them, so clang reports `t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:68:11: warning: variable 'probe' is not needed and will not be emitted [-Wunneeded-internal-declaration]` (run 39064711603, job 117492574143, log line 1374; I grepped the log). The warning is new in this PR: `git show 6198824246:t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp` has non-template users. The build has no -Werror, so the check stays green, but the PR adds a warning to the log of the lane that gates it. Smallest fix: move the whole fixture (`namespace {` at :53 through the fake definitions ending at :286) under the existing `#ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` that starts at :288; nothing in a TRON_AMX_DISPATCH-off binary references `amx_attn_h128g4::available()`, so the fakes are not needed there either. judged.rule: Wade check 14 (dead symbol) / check 16 (debug or diagnostic output that ships)
corrections: Minor range correction: the fake definitions end at :285 (the pv fake's closing brace) and the enclosing `}  // namespace tron::amx_attn_h128g4` is at :287, not :286; the `#ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` at :288 is right.

If re-homed under another reviewer: drop the "dead symbol" framing and the check 14/16 citations. `probe` is not dead at HEAD (readers at :186-237 and :258-282); it is unreferenced only in the TRON_AMX_DISPATCH-off build because every reader is an uninstantiated template. Keep the verified CI evidence (run 39064711603, job 117492574143, log line 1374) and the two fix options; both are consistent with HEAD (all amx_attn_h128g4 call sites in h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp sit under #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH at :254, :276, :477, :1528, :1630, :1681, :1872, so the fakes are unreferenced in an OFF build).

None of the facts need correcting. Optional strengthening for the comment: cite t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:22 as the in-tree precedent for wrapping the whole fixture (includes and all) in #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, which makes the "move the fixture under the ifdef" fix the idiom the sibling test already uses.
refutations: Facts hold, rule does not. (a) Scope: the warning is new in this diff. BASE t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:236-253 defines the three fakes as plain functions that read `probe`; HEAD :255-284 makes them templates (`template <size_t group_heads> requires(group_heads_ok(group_heads)) void pack_q_group_128x4(...) { ++probe.pack_calls;`), and the only other reader `exercise_page` is a template at HEAD :79-80, instantiated only inside the `#ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` block at :288-322. Check 16 (SKILL.md:136-150) triggers on a flipped `#define` debug switch, an added dump/log/trace call, or an always-on debug print, and its exclusion list ends with "t/."; a compiler diagnostic emitted by the gating lane is none of its triggers, and the file is under t/. No Wade check mentions build warnings (grep -i warning on the skill file returns nothing). So the finding is refuted as a Wade-code-review item. The underlying fact (a new -Wunneeded-internal-declaration warning in the gating Build Tron lane, introduced by this PR) is real and verified; if the orchestrator wants it posted, it belongs to a reviewer or skill whose rules cover compiler warnings in CI lanes, not to Wade checks 14/16.

judged.title: The transpose scratch `u` is declared `[4][4]` while the helper that receives it spells the same dimensions as `[TILE_ROWS_16 / ROWS_PER_LANE_4][ROWS_PER_LANE_4]`.
judged.body: Check 13 (a number in production code carries its role). The diff introduces `ROWS_PER_LANE_4` (:167) and uses `TILE_ROWS_16 / ROWS_PER_LANE_4` and `ROWS_PER_LANE_4` as the dimensions of the reference parameter at :171. The array that is passed to it is declared two lines below the hunk as `__m512 u[4][4];` (:233, a context line of the hunk at HEAD 224-233). A reader now sees two spellings of one array type and must work out that `TILE_ROWS_16 / ROWS_PER_LANE_4` is 4. A mismatch would be caught by the compiler (reference to array of exact bound), so the cost is reading, not correctness. Nit: `__m512 u[TILE_ROWS_16 / ROWS_PER_LANE_4][ROWS_PER_LANE_4];` at :233, matching the helper signature.
judged.rule: Wade check 13 (number carries its role)
judged.evidence:
171:     const __m512 (&u)[TILE_ROWS_16 / ROWS_PER_LANE_4][ROWS_PER_LANE_4],
233:     __m512 u[4][4];
refutations:
Pre-existing, unchanged SIMD line; Wade check 13 excludes it on two counts.

(a) Scope: `__m512 u[4][4];` at HEAD src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:233 is byte-identical to BASE line 188 (`git show 61988242…:src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp` line 188). In the diff it is a context line (pr5015.diff line 453, hunk `@@ -180,9 +224,10 @@`), not an added line. The diff did not make it wrong: the finder itself says the compiler enforces the bound ("the cost is reading, not correctness"). The sibling literals in the same unchanged block (HEAD:231 `for (int r = 0; r < 4; r++)`, HEAD:236 `row_group < 4`, HEAD:237-240 `(4 * row_group + k) * 16`) are equally unchanged, so renaming only the `u` bound would add a second spelling inside the block rather than remove one.

(b) Rule: Wade-code-review SKILL.md check 13 (line 121) triggers on "a bare literal above 1 in a changed function", and its procedure step 1 (line 124) is "Grep added lines, comments stripped, for literals above 1 the removed line lacked." Line 233 is not an added line and no removed line is paired with it. The do-not-fire list (line 130) explicitly excludes "unchanged lines unless the diff touches their replacing constant" and "SIMD (vector instruction) code". Nothing replaced the 4 in `u[4][4]`; `ROWS_PER_LANE_4` (HEAD:167) was introduced for the new helper's parameter at HEAD:171, not as a replacement constant for line 233. And the declaration sits inside an AVX-512 intrinsic transpose block (`_mm512_loadu_ps` / `_mm512_shuffle_f32x4`), which is the SIMD exclusion.

(c) Not answered in the PR body and not an issue #5021 name, so (c) does not apply; (a) and (b) alone refute it.

Line 233 `__m512 u[4][4];` is a context line the diff did not touch (it is on main unchanged). It sits inside an unpack block that is uniformly literal at HEAD and also untouched: `for (int r = 0; r < 4; r++)` (:231), `for (int row_group = 0; row_group < 4; row_group++)` (:236), `src + (4 * row_group + 0) * 16` (:237-240) and `s + r * 16` (:254). The only symbolic spelling is the new helper signature at :171. The compiler enforces the bound match (reference to array of exact extent), so there is no correctness defect; the cost is reading one division of two named constants. The proposed one-line fix would make the block mixed, not uniform: the array bounds would read `TILE_ROWS_16 / ROWS_PER_LANE_4` while the loops that fill it two lines below still say `row_group < 4` and `4 * row_group + k`. A uniform fix would have to rewrite :231-:254, which is unchanged kv_mul-4 code the PR body states on purpose is left instruction-identical to main; widening the diff there is out of this PR's scope. Per the task rule, an out-of-diff line is kept only when it is a real defect; a reading-cost nit on an unchanged literal that matches its unchanged neighbours is not one.

t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:316-318 and :330-332: the return precedes the SECTIONs

So the Wade rule yields no hit here; the finding is really a plain-English Rule 1 point (term not defined at first use), which is a different skill and not the rule named.
