Refuted on (b) and (c).

judged.title: The gate change admits every head-128 / kv_mul-16 model, and the body does not say whether Glimmer is the only served model of that shape.
judged.body: Check 25 (behavior change: on which input do the removed and the added line differ, and does the body say so). `shape_ok` at HEAD :163-165 now returns true for any model with head size 128 and kv_mul 16, with TRON_AMX_DISPATCH on. The body presents the change as Glimmer's shape (line 7) and measures Glimmer and llama-8b only. Any other ingested model with 16 query heads per KV head at head 128 (for example a Qwen3-235B-A22B-class geometry, 64 query heads over 4 KV heads) also moves its dense pages from the AVX dotter to AMX, with the RNE-versus-truncation numerics difference the Note describes and no measurement. Insufficient data: the tree does not list the served models' head geometries (README.models.md names none; ingested configs live outside the tree), so whether such a model exists in production is unknown. Ask: one sentence in Background saying either that Glimmer is the only served model with this shape, or naming the others and stating they are unmeasured.
judged.rule: Wade check 25 (silent behavior change) / check 6 (claim scope)
judged.evidence:
pr-body.md:7: Muse Glimmer 30B has 32 query heads over 2 KV heads at head size 128. Its kv_mul is therefore 16.
h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:163-164: constexpr bool shape_ok(size_t model_head_size, size_t model_kv_mul) noexcept { return model_head_size == HEAD_SIZE_128 && group_heads_ok(model_kv_mul);
corrections: (1) "with TRON_AMX_DISPATCH on" understates the gate: eligible = shape_ok && query_scalar_ok (iface :183-185), so a model of that shape moves to AMX only on an executor whose activation scalar is bf16 (tp*/perm_tp*/host_bf16), and only when available() holds; add "on a bf16-activation executor". (2) "the tree does not list the served models' head geometries (README.models.md names none; ingested configs live outside the tree)" should read "config/models.yaml lists the registered models by Hugging Face id (Glimmer at :684-711) but not their head geometries, so which other registered or production models have head 128 / kv_mul 16 cannot be read from the tree".
refutations: The hunk is in the diff (BASE amx_attn_iface.hpp:150 `model_kv_mul == GROUP_HEADS_4` -> HEAD :164 `group_heads_ok(model_kv_mul)`), so scope (a) passes. The finding fails on the rule (b). Check 25 fires only on a behavior change "unexplained in the body", and its do-not-fire list reads "a body or in-hunk sentence naming it". The input on which old and new differ is kv_mul 16 at head size 128, and the body names it in three places: line 3 ("accept ... 16 query heads per KV head"), line 9 ("On main the AMX kernels serve head size 128 with kv_mul 4 only, and the gate `shape_ok` refuses every other shape") and line 35 ("A model with any other kv_mul is refused by the gate"). The in-hunk comment at HEAD :161-162 ("the AMX kernels serve 128-dim heads with 4 or 16 query heads per KV head") and Note [AMX attention dispatch] at HEAD :23 ("head size 128 and kv_mul 4 or 16") name it too. The change is the PR's stated purpose (title: "serve kv_mul 16"), not a change presented as a refactor. Check 6 covers four subjects: (a) a compile-time type guarantee, (b) a timer or counter scope, (c) a [0]-read container count, (d) a twice-stated default. "Which served models have this shape" is none of them, and the body's claim is not wider than the code: the body says the kernels accept the shape "16 query heads per KV head" (line 3), which is exactly what HEAD :163-164 enforces. The finding argues the reverse (code wider than the measured set), which no check supports. The gate was shape-based at BASE as well (BASE :150 admitted any head-128 / kv_mul-4 model, not llama-8b by name), so admitting by shape rather than by model name is pre-existing behavior the diff did not introduce. The finder itself reports "Insufficient data" on whether any other kv_mul-16 / head-128 model is served, so the finding rests on a hypothetical input, not a named one as check 25 step 2 requires.

The body already states the behavior change in gate terms, not Glimmer terms. Line 3: "The AMX kernels accept ... 16 query heads per KV head, through one template parameter." Lines 34-35: "`group_heads_ok` lists 4 and 16, `shape_ok` uses it ... A model with any other kv_mul is refused by the gate." The header says the same at HEAD amx_attn_iface.hpp:13-14 ("The kernels serve head size 128 with kv_mul 4 or 16 (group_heads_ok)") and :23-24 (Note [AMX attention dispatch]: "a model with head size 128 and kv_mul 4 or 16"). So Wade check 25 (on which input does the new line differ, and does the body say so) is satisfied: the admitted set is stated as a shape, and the code at :163-164 matches it. Line 7 is Background motivation, not the claim of scope. The gate was shape-based on main too (head 128, kv_mul 4 admitted llama-8b, qwen3-4b and any other such model) and no PR body listed the served models per shape; the RNE-vs-truncation difference (iface :67, :80) is a property of the kernel the gate already carries for kv_mul 4, not something this PR introduces per model. The finder's example model (a 64/4-head geometry) is hypothetical and the finder itself marks the production inventory as Insufficient data from the tree, so the author cannot verify the requested sentence from the repo either; a sentence about which models production serves today would go stale and is not a PR-body obligation. Consequence hypothetical, body already states the scope: not worth a comment.

composed.review_body:
Wade-code-review: Short version. I checked every touched file at HEAD 5061623a34 against the 35 Wade-code-review checks (dead symbols, debug switches, comment vs code, magic literals, names, silent fallbacks, gated or duplicate tests, PR-body claims and CI lanes). The review holds 16 findings: 7 inline comments and 9 body items, with 2 should-fix items (the 16-head kernel cases run on no gating CI lane, and a new compiler warning on the gating lane) and the rest nits or fwiw. Verdict for this reviewer: approve with nits, since neither should-fix item blocks and both have a small repair.

Words used here: kv_mul = query heads per KV head. group_heads = the template parameter carrying kv_mul into the AMX kernels. A lane = one CI workflow file with its trigger block and configure line. pr-body.md = the PR description as a GitHub reader sees it.

Findings that are not anchored to a diff line:

- Wade-code-review: t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:68 [should-fix]. The gating Build Tron job now warns `t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:68:11: warning: variable 'probe' is not needed and will not be emitted [-Wunneeded-internal-declaration]` (run 39064711603, job 117492574143, log line 1374). The warning is new in this PR. At BASE the three fakes were plain functions that read `probe` (BASE :236-253). At HEAD every reader sits inside a template: the fakes at :255-285 and `exercise_page` at :79-241. On Build Tron (nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix, TRON_AMX_DISPATCH absent, CMakeLists.txt:46 defaults it OFF) nothing instantiates them. The build has no -Werror, so the check stays green, but the PR adds a warning to the log of the lane that gates it. `probe` is not dead at HEAD (readers at :186-237 and :258-282), and no Wade check covers compiler warnings, so this is a plain build-hygiene item. Smallest fix: move the whole fixture (`namespace {` at :53 through the fake definitions ending at :285 and the closing `}  // namespace tron::amx_attn_h128g4` at :287) under the `#ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` at :288. Nothing in an OFF build references `amx_attn_h128g4::available()` (every call site in h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp sits under that ifdef at :254, :276, :477, :1528, :1630, :1681, :1872), and t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:22 already wraps its whole fixture that way. One-line alternative: `[[maybe_unused]] amx_probe probe;`.

- Wade-code-review: pr-body.md:108 and :94 [nit]. The comparator row cites `nightly GitHub Actions run 38999609242 (2026-10-17)` without its repository. That run is not in positron-ai/tron (`gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/actions/runs/38999609242` returns 404), and no workflow under .github/workflows at HEAD mentions Glimmer (Glimmer appears only in bin/ci/prime_hf_models.py, bin/ci/test_prime_hf_models.py and config/{models.yaml,test-benchmarks.json,test_model_definitions.py}, none of which is a workflow). The run is positron-ai/systems_test, workflow "System CI (Rinzler 72-core Intel system OCI version)", job system_ci, event schedule. Its performance phase completed at 05:33 UTC. The Glimmer tp4 row is the log line `Running averages: TTFT=3696, TPS=78.69` from root.benchmark_tps (80 samples, TPS sd 0.48, TTFT sd 188 ms). The run's overall conclusion is failure, from the later soak phase (13:11 UTC, "FPGA 2 (99.74 Watts) below minimum threshold (100 Watts)"), unrelated to the perf row. A reader cannot resolve the 78.69 TPS / 3697 ms comparator from the body, and the base arm at :109 reproduces it, so the row matters. Ask: at :94 write "The nightly CI perf phase (positron-ai/systems_test, workflow System CI) runs ...", at :108 link the run with its repository and workflow name, and name the log line or summary the row comes from. The log's final running average prints TTFT 3696 ms while the row says 3697 ms, and the run has no artifacts, so the body should say where 3697 comes from.

- Wade-code-review: pr-body.md:46, :85, :94, :104 [nit]. Two items on line 46. (1) The Verification section names raw-result files a GitHub reader cannot open: :46 `Raw results: rt-results.txt, attn-stats-compare.md, tests.txt and local-obj-compare/ (result set glimmer-20261016)`, :85 `(the rows are in rt-results.txt)`, :94 `summary.md records the harness settings`, :104 `Raw results: perf.json per pass (every request) and summary.md (result set glimci-20261017)`. None is in the repository at HEAD (`git ls-tree -r HEAD` has no rt-results.txt, attn-stats-compare.md, tests.txt, local-obj-compare or glimci-20261017) and none is attached to the PR. Each reference costs the reader a lookup that ends nowhere. Please drop the file names, or replace each with a link a GitHub reader can open, and keep the commit id, the dates and the outcome clauses. Optional: the prefill rows summarised at :85 ("by 0.6 to 8.7 % with FPGA attention, by 1.3 to 14.8 % with CPU attention") have no row in the body. If you want them checkable without the raw file, two prefill columns on the decode table at :73-83 would do it. (2) :46 says the runtron cells ran `on delphi-3bda, our half`. "our half" is a local machine-sharing convention that nothing in the repository or the body defines (plain-English rule: define a term at first use). It does carry a condition: it separates the runtron cells (one socket) from the CI cells on "the whole of delphi-3bda" at :96, which a reader comparing the tp4 rows at :77 and :113 needs. Suggested replacement: "on one socket of delphi-3bda (half of its 8 FPGA cards; the other socket was not used by these runs)". Do not write that the other half was idle unless the raw results record it.

- Wade-code-review: pr-body.md:3 and :63 [nit]. The Short version says `the kv_mul-4 kernels emit the same instructions as on main`. The body's own review guide at :42 and the Verification row at :63 narrow that: the pack and QK objects are identical, and `weights_times_v_128x4` differs in the thread-local access model (main local-dynamic, branch general-dynamic) and in register allocation across the tile loop (main %rsi/%rcx/%rdx/%rax, branch %rdi/%rax/%rsi/%rcx). The cause is the `thread_local` P scratch at src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:284, which has vague linkage now that the function is a template. So the headline covers three kernels and the evidence covers two. The rescue clause at :63, `The linker rewrites both to the same code`, has no measurement behind it: the compare described at :46 was on object files at -O3, before linking, and a linker rewrites relocations, not register choices. Ask for consistency between :3 and :42/:63, keeping the Short version free of implementation detail: at :3 write "and the kv_mul-4 pack and QK kernels emit the same instructions as on main", and at :63 drop the linker clause or replace it with "Both relax to local-exec TLS when linked into the executable. Equivalent, not compared byte for byte on the linked runtron".

- Wade-code-review: pr-body.md:55 [nit]. `CI runs it` (clang-format) is right: the GCP Nix Lint job (gcp-nix.yml:54, bin/ci/run-lint-checks.sh) runs clang-format-19 (flake.nix:2322-2323). It is the body's only CI sentence, and no sentence says what the required checks compile. The gating lane is GCP Nix (gcp-nix.yml, on: push to main, pull_request, merge_group). Its build recipe nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix:79-101 passes no TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, and CMakeLists.txt:46 defaults the option OFF. So on that lane src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp is not compiled, every self_attention.hpp hunk of this PR sits under `#ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` (:276, :1528, :1681), and the two AMX test binaries run their placeholder cases (t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:344, t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:319). Outside the PR checks, the option is set only by cmake-single-platform.yml:355 (workflow_dispatch and workflow_call) and by the deb preset (CMakePresets.json:68) that the nightly publish-deb build on main uses. So the kernels reach CI only through the nightly deb perf phase after merge, and the AMX host tests of this PR run nowhere in CI. A reader who takes the 12 green required checks as execution of the 16-head kernels is wrong. Please add under Builds and tests: "The PR's required checks (GCP Nix) build without TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, so they compile none of the AMX code and run the placeholder test cases. Every run of the kernels in this section is the author's run on delphi-3bda." See also the inline comment at t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:323.

- Wade-code-review: pr-body.md:35 [nit]. `A caller with any other size fails to link` names the wrong mechanism. Each kernel declaration carries `requires(group_heads_ok(group_heads))` (h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:203, :243, :257), and `group_heads_ok` at :152-154 is true for 4 and 16 only. A call such as `pack_q_group_128x4<8>(...)` has no viable candidate and fails to compile ("no matching function ... constraints not satisfied"). It never reaches the linker. The explicit instantiation list at src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:334-354 is the link-time backstop that matters only if the constraint were removed. The sentence sends a reviewer to look for a link error that cannot happen. Replacement: "A caller with any other size fails to compile: the requires clause on each kernel (amx_attn_iface.hpp:203, :243, :257) has no match. The instantiation list is the link-time backstop and must stay equal to group_heads_ok."

- Wade-code-review: pr-body.md:28 [nit] (check 17, a comment's identifiers match the line they describe). The review guide says row `4*l + k` of `s` uses the `vshufps` selector `0x88`. The helper at src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:178-181 calls `_mm512_shuffle_f32x4`, which assembles to VSHUFF32X4 (a 128-bit lane shuffle). VSHUFPS is a different instruction (a 32-bit element shuffle inside each 128-bit lane) and would not implement the lane selection the comment at :155-162 describes. Checked: g++ -mavx512f compiles `_mm512_shuffle_f32x4(a, b, 0x88)` to `vshuff32x4 $0x88` and `_mm512_shuffle_ps` to `vshufps $0x88`. A reviewer who greps the disassembly for vshufps finds nothing, while :62 already counts `vshuf` shuffles, which matches vshuff32x4. Suggested text: "uses the `_mm512_shuffle_f32x4` (vshuff32x4) selector `0x88` ...". The selector arithmetic itself checks out: after the unpack stages, 128-bit lane l of `u[row_group][k]` holds tile column 4*l + k, 0x88 picks lanes {0,2} and 0xdd lanes {1,3} of each input, so lane bit 0 drives stage 3 and bit 1 drives stage 4.

- Wade-code-review: pr-body.md:53 [nit] (check 8, result rows match the reviewed head). The AMX-off row reads `t_amx_numerics 4,110 / 4 pass, 2 sections skipped with "AMX unavailable on this host"`. At HEAD the `available()` return sits in the TEST_CASE body above the SECTIONs (t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:316-318 and :330-332), and each case holds two SECTIONs (:320-325, :334-339). So an AMX-off run returns early from 2 test cases, which hold 4 sections, not from 2 sections. "4 pass" matches the log (Catch2 reports a case that returns after WARN as passed) and stays. The quoted text is the shared prefix of the two WARN messages at :317 and :331 ("... - QK precision check skipped", "... - PV precision check skipped"). Replacement: `t_amx_numerics 4,110 / 4 pass. The QK and PV cases (2 of 4 cases, 4 SECTIONs between them) return early with WARN "AMX unavailable on this host" (the precision checks need the kernel)`.

comments.body:
Wade-code-review: `group_heads_ok` names its parameter `g` while the sibling gate spells its parameter out [nit]. HEAD line 152 reads `constexpr bool group_heads_ok(size_t g) noexcept {`. Eleven lines below, `shape_ok(size_t model_head_size, size_t model_kv_mul)` (:163) uses full names, and every call site passes a spelled name: `group_heads_ok(model_kv_mul)` at :164 and `requires(group_heads_ok(group_heads))` at :203, :243, :257. `g` is the only one-letter parameter in the header. A reader must map `g` to group_heads (query heads per KV head) by themselves. This is a consistency point, not a rule hit: `group_heads` is a name this PR introduces, so there is no repository spelling that `g` abbreviates. Proposed replacement for line 152:

```suggestion
constexpr bool group_heads_ok(size_t group_heads) noexcept {
```

Line 153 then becomes `  return group_heads == GROUP_HEADS_4 || group_heads == GROUP_HEADS_16;`.

Wade-code-review: `inline` on `store_transposed_rows` changes nothing [fwiw]. HEAD :170 reads `inline void store_transposed_rows(` under `template <int lane>` at :169, inside the anonymous namespace opened at :148 and closed at :185. The one-definition rule already lets a function template be defined in every translation unit, which is the allowance `inline` grants a plain function. The anonymous namespace gives it internal linkage anyway. So deleting `inline` changes no linkage, no type and no build. The specifier is not needed for inlining either: each instantiation `store_transposed_rows<0..3>` has a single call site (:255, :257-259) inside an internal-linkage kernel, and clang at -O3 inlines such called-once functions with or without the hint. The PR body's object compare shows it folded into `qk_rowmajor_128x4` (205 instructions, identical to main). The file's other anonymous-namespace function, `detect_and_request()` at :86, carries no `inline`, so dropping it matches the file's own idiom. No action needed.

Wade-code-review: the 16-head QK and PV sections execute on no CI lane that gates this PR, so the only execution is the author's local run [should-fix] (check 3A, a test must run and reach its assertion). A lane is one CI workflow file. The required checks come from gcp-nix.yml (trigger `pull_request`, :13). Its Build Tron job builds from nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix, whose cmake_args (:79-100) carry no `-DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH`, and CMakeLists.txt:46 defaults the option OFF. So on that lane this file compiles only the stub at :342-346, and the GCP Nix run at HEAD (run 39064711603, job 117495894283) prints `passed t_amx_numerics inst 0,8 0.5s` for that stub. The only lane that sets `-DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON` is cmake-single-platform.yml:355. It has no `push` or `pull_request` trigger (:2-8) and runs on `[self-hosted, fpga, test, avx512]` (:381), a label set that includes the AMD runners without AMX. There both kernel cases exit at :316-319 and :330-333 with a WARN and the binary still reports passed. So a wrong 16-head store (for example the two selectors at src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:174-175 swapped) keeps every required check green. The lane gap predates this PR, so this is a non-blocking ask. Either repair answers it: (a) one sentence under Builds and tests saying the required checks compile the AMX cases out and the delphi-3bda run is the execution of the 16-head sections. (b) Replace `WARN(...); return;` at :317-318 and :331-332 with Catch2's `SKIP("AMX unavailable on this host")` (Catch2 is v3.7.1 per cmake/versions.cmake:26, and t/t_disk_cache.cpp:182 already uses SKIP), so Catch2's own summary on an AMD runner counts the two cases as skipped instead of passed. The slice line stays `passed`, since the two non-gated cases keep the exit code at 0, and the body's AMX-off row would then say "2 test cases skipped".

Wade-code-review: the second round of the 16-head dispatch section repeats what the 4-head section's second round already observes [nit] (check 4, same experiment run twice). HEAD :301-302 read `exercise_page<host_bf16, amx_attn_h128g4::GROUP_HEADS_16>(page_size, /*repeat=*/true);`. Round 0 of this section is distinct: it observes `probe.pack_group_heads == 16` and its two sibling counters (:202-204) and the 16 x 128 packed values with a per-head offset (:145-148, :237). A call site that hard-coded `GROUP_HEADS_4` instead of the model's kv_mul (query heads per KV head) at self_attention.hpp:1696, :1763 or :1791 fails here and nowhere else. Round 1 observes only that a second `apply_page_range` call packs again (:177-186). The state it probes is the per-call bitset `amx_packed` (self_attention.hpp:1549), which does not depend on the group size, and the 4-head section at :292-295 already observes it. Its values at :181 carry no per-head offset, so it observes less than round 0. No break fails the 16-head round 1 and passes both the 4-head round 1 and the 16-head round 0. Cost is about 2,100 extra REQUIREs per run, well under a second, so a nit. Proposed edit: `exercise_page<host_bf16, amx_attn_h128g4::GROUP_HEADS_16>(page_size);` and drop the clause `; a second call with new queries packs again` from the section name at :299-300. The header at :17-18 needs no change. The body's Verification row `t_amx_dispatch_dtype 5,756 / 1 pass` counts assertions and must be refreshed after the change.

Wade-code-review: the comment says the kv_mul-4 names "are kept" but points at no tracker, while the PR body says issue #5021 owns the rename [fwiw]. HEAD :14-16 read `// 128 with kv_mul 4 or 16 (group_heads_ok). The namespace name` / `// amx_attn_h128g4 and the _128x4 suffix of every kernel record the first` / `// shape, kv_mul 4, and are kept.` (kv_mul = query heads per KV head). This is not about the names themselves. A reader of the header alone cannot tell whether the mismatch is permanent or tracked. The form `TODO(#4361):` at h/common/numerics/bf16.hpp:127 is the in-tree precedent. Proposed replacement for line 16:

```suggestion
// shape, kv_mul 4. TODO(#5021): rename them.
```

kept.title: The lane-bit masks 1 and 2 in store_transposed_rows are unnamed numeric literals.
kept.rule: cpp-coding-guide / Named values: literals other than 0 and alignas go in named declarations
kept.evidence:
174:  constexpr int pair_sel = (lane & 1) ? LANES_ODD_0XDD : LANES_EVEN_0X88;
175:  constexpr int quad_sel = (lane & 2) ? LANES_ODD_0XDD : LANES_EVEN_0X88;
corrections: One sentence overstates: "the masks are the only bare numbers left in the helper" is not literally true. Lines 178-179 also index `u[0][k]`, `u[1][k]`, `u[2][k]`, `u[3][k]` with bare 1, 2, 3 (positions in the 4-entry row-group array). Those are plain array positions, not encoded rules, so the finding can leave them out, but the comment should say "the masks are the only bare numbers that encode a rule" (or similar) instead of "the only bare numbers".

Drop the closing parenthetical "(the uppercase names are the subject of the next finding)": a posted inline comment has no "next finding", and the uppercase rename belongs to its own comment. Keep the proposed replacement either with the current lowercase pair_sel/quad_sel or state plainly that the uppercase spelling is a separate point.

Two small additions so the comment is accurate and does not over-claim: (1) say the pre-existing cpuid bit tests at HEAD lines 94 and 98 (`(d >> 22) & 1`, `3u << 17`) also use bare masks but are untouched by the diff and out of scope, so the "only bare numbers left in the helper" claim is scoped to store_transposed_rows, not the file; (2) note that jhan's recorded exception (2026-10-02) covers a shift's `1` and mask-minus-one arithmetic only, so this case is reported rather than exempted. Optionally, prefer names that say what the value is and avoid two digits in one name (LANE_BIT0_MASK_1 reads as bit 0 and value 1): e.g. `constexpr int STAGE3_LANE_BIT_1 = 1;` and `constexpr int STAGE4_LANE_BIT_2 = 2;`, which keep the NAME_<value> suffix and tie each mask to the stage named in the comment at lines 157-160.

kept.title: The constexpr locals pair_sel and quad_sel are not in uppercase.
kept.rule: cpp-coding-guide / Named values: constexpr variables use uppercase letters and underscores
kept.evidence:
174:  constexpr int pair_sel = (lane & 1) ? LANES_ODD_0XDD : LANES_EVEN_0X88;
175:  constexpr int quad_sel = (lane & 2) ? LANES_ODD_0XDD : LANES_EVEN_0X88;
corrections: Two fixes to the comment text. (1) The proposed replacement uses LANE_BIT0_MASK_1 and LANE_BIT1_MASK_2, which do not exist anywhere in the worktree (grep over src/tron/kernels and h/tron/kernels finds no LANE_BIT); the comment must either add their declarations (e.g. `constexpr int LANE_BIT0_MASK_1 = 1; constexpr int LANE_BIT1_MASK_2 = 2;` in the anonymous namespace next to LANES_EVEN_0X88) or keep `lane & 1` / `lane & 2` and limit the ask to the uppercase rename. (2) The sentence "this file already writes a derived function-local constexpr in uppercase ... so the lowercase spelling also departs from the file's own idiom" is overstated: the file also has a pre-existing lowercase namespace-scope constexpr, `constexpr unsigned long xfeature_xtiledata = 18;` [amx_attn.cpp:29, outside the diff], so the file's idiom is not uniform. Rest the finding on the guide rule alone, or say "the file's only other function-local constexpr (line 294) is uppercase".

Two text fixes before posting. (1) The proposed replacement uses `LANE_BIT0_MASK_1` and `LANE_BIT1_MASK_2`, which do not exist in the file; either drop them and keep `(lane & 1)` / `(lane & 2)` so the comment stays on the uppercase rule alone, or state explicitly that the replacement also adds `constexpr int LANE_BIT0_MASK_1 = 1;` and `constexpr int LANE_BIT1_MASK_2 = 2;` to the anonymous namespace (that would be a separate point under the "Keep other literals, including `1`, in named declarations" rule, SKILL.md:20). (2) The sentence "departs from the file's own idiom" is slightly overstated: the file also has a pre-existing lowercase `constexpr unsigned long xfeature_xtiledata = 18;` at HEAD:29 (unchanged from BASE). judged.title: The P-scratch comment justifies per-instantiation isolation with a hazard that does not exist for the rows callers read.
judged.body: Rule applied: "State the invariant, ownership rule, ordering requirement, or failure mode that motivates the implementation" and "Avoid ... a comment that merely restates the code" (positron-code-review, Preserve the technical reason). The added sentences at HEAD lines 279-283 say: "A function template's static locals exist once per specialization. This scratch therefore belongs to the 4-head or the 16-head instantiation only, and a 4-head call never sees a 16-head call's rows." A reader looks for the hazard this isolation prevents and finds none in the code. By the kernel's own contract, output row i of a tile multiply comes from row i of the A operand (amx_attn_iface.hpp:104-105), and P is the A operand here (line 301, `_tile_loadd(P_TILE_4, &P[0][...])`). So stale 16-head weights in P rows 4..15 could only change rows 4..15 of `o`, which every caller ignores (self_attention.hpp:1794-1797 reads offsets below operation_kv_mul; t_amx_numerics.cpp:274 reads qi below group_heads). The isolation is a true C++ fact, but as written it reads as the reason the 4-head path stays correct, and the PR body repeats it as such ("The thread_local P scratch is one per instantiation" under "Is the kv_mul-4 path unchanged?"). Reading cost: a reviewer spends time hunting for the dependency between the two instantiations. Proposed fix (smallest change that keeps the fact and adds its consequence): replace lines 279-283 with "A function template's static locals exist once per specialization, so this scratch is separate for the 4-head and the 16-head instantiation. That separation changes nothing a caller reads: P row i feeds only output row i, and callers read rows 0..group_heads-1 of `o`. For 16 heads every row is written, so there is no padding." Alternatively drop the two isolation sentences.
judged.rule: positron-code-review: Preserve the technical reason (state the failure mode; do not restate the code)
judged.evidence:
279:  // the padded tile rows contribute nothing. A function template's static
280:  // locals exist once per specialization. This scratch therefore belongs to
281:  // the 4-head or the 16-head instantiation only, and a 4-head call never
282:  // sees a 16-head call's rows. For 16 heads every row is written, so there
283:  // is no padding.
corrections: Minor: the proposed replacement says "replace lines 279-283", but line 279 begins with the tail of the previous sentence ("the padded tile rows contribute nothing."). The fix should replace only from "A function template's static" (mid-line 279) through line 283, keeping that clause. Everything else in the comment text checks out.

If the comment is posted under a different reviewer rule, drop the sentence "A reader looks for the hazard this isolation prevents and finds none in the code": the hazard is the documented invariant that rows group_heads..15 of P stay zero after thread init (amx_attn.cpp:277-279) and that rows group_heads..15 of `o` are products of those zero rows (amx_attn_iface.hpp:103-105); a shared scratch would break both statements for a 4-head call that follows a 16-head call on the same thread, even though no caller reads those rows. Also do not attribute the finding to positron-code-review; that skill covers only review-narration references, and this comment contains none.
refutations: Lens (a) passes: the sentences at HEAD src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:279-283 ("A function template's static locals exist once per specialization ... a 4-head call never sees a 16-head call's rows") are new in this diff; BASE (git show 6198824246:src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp, lines 228-231) ends the comment at "contribute nothing." Lens (b) fails, and that refutes the finding. The named rule lives in ~/.claude/skills/positron-code-review/SKILL.md, whose scope is "temporary pull-request review narration": it flags "Pull-request review rounds or numbered review passes", "Reviewer-specific comment labels", and "Statements that a reviewer requested the code, without the technical reason", and it states "This skill supplies one focused comment-quality check. It does not prescribe a broader correctness review." The "Preserve the technical reason" section the finder quotes says what to keep WHEN removing a review-process reference ("Remove the review-process reference while retaining the useful explanation ... Avoid replacing review narration with a comment that merely restates the code"). HEAD lines 276-283 contain no review-round, reviewer-label or "as requested" reference, so there is no narration to replace and the rule does not reach this comment. The finding is a general comment-quality or reasoning-clarity complaint, which the skill explicitly disclaims. Lens (c): the PR body section "Is the kv_mul-4 path unchanged?" (pr-body.md lines 39-42) already states "The thread_local P scratch is one per instantiation" with the object-compare and llama-8b cell as evidence, so the per-instantiation fact is answered there; the finding adds only a framing preference. Secondary factual weakness in the comment text: the claim that a reader "finds none in the code" is not accurate. The interface contract at h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:103-105 documents that "Rows group_heads..15 of `o` are the products of the kernel's zero padding rows of P", and amx_attn.cpp:277-279 states rows group_heads..15 are "never written after thread init". A scratch shared across the two instantiations would make both statements false for a 4-head call after a 16-head call on the same thread (rows 4..15 would hold stale 16-head weights). The isolation sentences therefore support a documented invariant, even though callers (self_attention.hpp:1794-1797, t_amx_numerics.cpp:274) only read rows below group_heads. The line anchor 281 is inside the diff range [274,288] and the quoted text matches HEAD, so no line correction.

The two isolation sentences are not a free-floating justification; they back the claim immediately before them. HEAD src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:277-279 says "rows group_heads..15 are zero padding (never written after thread init)". On BASE (amx_attn.cpp:228-232) that claim was trivially true: one function, one thread_local. At HEAD there are two instantiations (amx_attn.cpp:343-352), and a reviewer's natural question is "does a 16-head call on the same thread write rows 4..15 of the 4-head scratch, making 'never written after thread init' false?" Lines 279-282 answer exactly that question. That is a stated reason, not a restatement of code, so the cited rule is not violated.

The isolation also has a documented consumer the finder missed: the interface contract at h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:104-105 says "Rows group_heads..15 of `o` are the products of the kernel's zero padding rows of P". A shared scratch would make rows 4..15 of `o` stale 16-head products after a 16-head call on the same thread (t_amx_numerics.cpp:336-341 runs check_pv<4> then check_pv<16> on one thread), and that sentence of the contract would be false. Per-instantiation storage keeps it literally true. The finder is right that no caller reads those rows (self_attention.hpp:1794-1797, t_amx_numerics.cpp:274), but the comment never claims caller correctness depends on the isolation; the finder's reading "as the reason the 4-head path stays correct" is an over-reading of "a 4-head call never sees a 16-head call's rows", which is about the scratch contents.

The PR-body sentence sits under "Is the kv_mul-4 path unchanged?" (pr-body.md:39-41). "One per instantiation" there means the 4-head instantiation's P has the same contents as main's (zero rows 4..15, written rows 0..3), which is a correct "unchanged" statement, not a correctness dependency.

The proposed fix would compile and format, but its added sentence ("P row i feeds only output row i, and callers read rows 0..group_heads-1 of `o`") duplicates Note [Tile stores write 16 rows] at amx_attn_iface.hpp:104-106, which the kernel comment already points to at amx_attn.cpp:274 ("see Note [Tile stores write 16 rows]"). Dropping the two sentences instead would leave "never written after thread init" unexplained under two instantiations. The stated reading cost is hypothetical; the comment names what it preserves in the sentence before it. Not worth a review comment even at fwiw.

151: // the 16 x 16 transpose (stage 1 interleaves 32-bit values, stage 2 interleaves
152: // 64-bit pairs), 128-bit lane `lane` (0..3) of u[row_group][k] holds tile

kept.title: The "padding stays zero" claim holds only while one group size uses a worker's pack slots; the result does not depend on it, so the comment states a stronger precondition than the kernel needs.
kept.body: Skill rule: trace the changed behavior beyond the diff (consumers of the packed-Q slot) and separate future risks from defects. The comment says the pack slots' padding "stays zero" because the packer "writes only the kv_mul live columns" [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1552-1554]. The slot vector `attn[scratchpad].amx_qpack` is one per worker scratchpad and is shared by every attention operation of the model state [line 1544]. A 16-head pack writes all 16 columns of every panel [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:138-139: `for (size_t q_head = 0; q_head < group_heads; q_head++)`, `dst = packed + ((step * 16 + dim_pair) * 16 + q_head) * 2`]. So in a model whose attention kernels mix kv_mul 16 and kv_mul 4 at head size 128, a later 4-head pack of the same slot would leave columns 4..15 holding the 16-head values, and the stated precondition of pack_q_group_128x4 ("columns group_heads..15 of every panel already zero" [h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:193]) would be violated. Consequence today: none. Each column of the QK result tile depends on its own packed-Q column only (`_tile_dpbf16ps` accumulates K[token].Q[column]), and the transposing store writes rows 0..group_heads-1 only [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:255-260], so stale padding columns produce discarded values. The PV scratch P is one per instantiation [amx_attn.cpp:284], so it is not shared either. No in-repo plugin has two kernels of different kv_mul at head 128 (llama.hpp declares one kernel [h/tron/plugins/llama.hpp:200-202]; the ingested Glimmer plugin has one geometry per the PR body), so the condition is not reachable now. Evidence strength: high that the condition is unreachable today, high that the result is unaffected if it were reached. Suggested fix (comment only, both sites): say what the kernel actually relies on. For example at line 1552: "resize() zero-fills new slots. The packer writes columns 0..kv_mul-1 of each slot; the QK kernel's result rows depend on those columns only, so whatever the other columns hold does not reach the scores." And drop "already zero" from the pack contract at amx_attn_iface.hpp:193-196, or keep it and add that a model with two group sizes would not satisfy it. Discriminating check: in t_amx_numerics check_qk<GROUP_HEADS_4>, fill columns 4..15 of q_packed with nonzero bf16 values before the kernel call and keep the row 0..3 dotter comparison; it passes today, which shows the precondition is not load-bearing.
kept.rule: Trace consumers beyond the diff; separate design choices and future risks from current defects
kept.evidence:
1552:        // resize() zero-fills new slots and the packer writes only the kv_mul
1553:        // live columns of each slot, so the padding it relies on stays zero
1554:        // (see the pack contract in amx_attn_iface.hpp).
refutations: The finding's own text says the consequence is none and the condition is unreachable; the verification shows it is unreachable by ownership, not only by today's plugin set. The pack slots live in `std::vector<attn_accum> attn;` [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:453], a member of `self_attention<model>::state` [line 236], and one `self_attention<model>` instance has one `geometry`, so one kv_mul: `constexpr bool amx_eligible = amx_attn_h128g4::eligible<...>(geometry.kv.head_size, geometry.kv_mul());` [lines 1537-1539]. Two kernels with different kv_mul would be two self_attention instances with two separate `attn` vectors, so a 4-head pack can never land on a slot that a 16-head pack wrote. The comment at lines 1552-1554 ("resize() zero-fills new slots and the packer writes only the kv_mul live columns ... so the padding it relies on stays zero") is therefore true as written, and the contract at amx_attn_iface.hpp:192-196 already handles the 16-head case explicitly ("For 16 heads every column is written, so that precondition is empty"). That the QK kernel would also tolerate nonzero padding (each `_tile_dpbf16ps` column depends on its own packed column, and `store_transposed_rows<1..3>` run only for GROUP_HEADS_16 [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:255-260]) makes the zero-padding contract conservative, which is a legitimate design choice, not a defect. The proposed fix would weaken a contract that a test checks (`REQUIRE(got == 0);  // padding columns stay untouched` [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:150]) and would move kernel-internal reasoning into the shared file self_attention.hpp, for no behavioral gain. Not worth a reviewer comment.

kept.title: The gate test checks shapes just outside the old limit (kv_mul 2, 8; head 64 with 4 heads) but none just outside the new upper limit (kv_mul 32, or head 64 with 16 heads).
kept.body: Rule: "Boundary model shapes: check dimensions at supported limits and just outside them. Unsupported dimensions should trigger the intended rejection." HEAD lines 113-122 assert eligible for (128, 4) and (128, 16), and refuse (128, 2), (128, 8) and (64, 4). Nothing refuses a kv_mul above 16 or a wrong head size paired with the new group size. A deliberate semantic break that the current rows would not catch: changing group_heads_ok to `g == GROUP_HEADS_4 || g >= GROUP_HEADS_16` (or `g % 16 == 0`) keeps every existing STATIC_REQUIRE green while admitting kv_mul 32, for which no kernel is instantiated (link error at best, in a model that reaches the dispatch). Proposed fix, two lines after line 121: `constexpr size_t KV_MUL_32 = 32;` `STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE(eligible<tron::bf16>(HEAD_SIZE_128, KV_MUL_32));` and `STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE(eligible<tron::bf16>(64, GROUP_HEADS_16));`. Cost: compile-time only.

Also the body says "two lines after line 121" but proposes three statements (a constant and two STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE); say "three lines" or drop the count.

Keep only the kv_mul-32 row; drop the eligible<tron::bf16>(64, GROUP_HEADS_16) row (shape_ok at amx_attn_iface.hpp:163-165 is a plain AND, and line 122 already covers the head check). Suggested text after line 121: `constexpr size_t KV_MUL_32 = 32;` then `STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE(eligible<tron::bf16>(HEAD_SIZE_128, KV_MUL_32));`, with the comment on lines 118-119 extended to say "and nothing above 16". Soften the consequence: no tron model has kv_mul 32 today, so the row guards a future edit of group_heads_ok (amx_attn_iface.hpp:152-154) rather than a current defect; the link-error claim holds (templates declared in the header, instantiated only at amx_attn.cpp:333-350).

judged.title: The 16-head dispatch section uses one KV head, so the group offset into q (kv_head * 16 * 128) is never exercised with the new group size.
judged.body: Skill rule: "Does its fake retain the information that could be wrong?" and "Boundary model shapes". The dispatch test drives the production apply_page_range with `constexpr size_t n_kv_heads = 1;` [t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:82], for the 4-head and the 16-head section alike. With one KV head, kv_head is always 0, so the packer always receives `q.data + 0` [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1696-1697: `pack_q_group_128x4<geometry.kv_mul()>(q.data + kv_head * geometry.kv_mul() * geometry.kv.head_size, slot)`]. The production model (Muse Glimmer, 2 KV heads) packs kv_head 1 from offset 16 * 128 = 2048 elements, a value no test computes. The fake pack records the group's values (`probe.q[i] = static_cast<float>(input[i])`, line 261) and the per-head offsets in `expected` (lines 145-148) would catch a wrong group base, but only if a kv_head other than 0 ever reaches the pack. Evidence strength: low for a current defect (the offset expression is unchanged by the diff and is generic in kv_mul), medium as a coverage gap for the new shape. Discriminating check: add a section with `n_kv_heads = 2`, `n_heads = 32` (Glimmer's shape) and have the fake record, per pack call, the first value of the group; require the kv_head-1 pack to see `expected[16 * 128]`. A wrong base (for example `kv_head * GROUP_HEADS_4 * head_size` left over from the 4-head era) would then fail; today it would pass.
judged.rule: Review the tests: does the fake retain the information that could be wrong; boundary model shapes
judged.evidence:
82:  constexpr size_t n_kv_heads = 1;
84:  constexpr attention_geometry geometry{n_heads, kv_geometry{n_kv_heads, head_size}};
corrections: If posted anyway, the comment must say that `n_kv_heads = 1` (HEAD line 82) and the `q.data + kv_head * geometry.kv_mul() * geometry.kv.head_size` base (self_attention.hpp:1697) both predate this PR unchanged, and must drop the "left over from the 4-head era" hypothetical, since HEAD already computes the base from geometry.kv_mul().
refutations: Scope: the one-KV-head fixture is pre-existing, not introduced by this diff. At BASE the test already had `constexpr size_t n_heads = 4;` and `constexpr size_t n_kv_heads = 1;` (BASE t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:73-74); the diff only turned n_heads into a template parameter and kept `constexpr size_t n_kv_heads = 1;` (HEAD line 82). The production offset the finding worries about is also unchanged: BASE h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1696-1697 reads `amx_attn_h128g4::pack_q_group_128x4(q.data + kv_head * geometry.kv_mul() * geometry.kv.head_size, slot);` and HEAD 1696-1697 reads the same with only `<geometry.kv_mul()>` added as a template argument. So kv_head > 0 was equally unexercised for group size 4 before the PR, and the hypothetical defect the finder's discriminating check targets (`kv_head * GROUP_HEADS_4 * head_size` left over) does not exist at HEAD, where the base is written in terms of `geometry.kv_mul()`. The finder itself rates the evidence "low for a current defect". Rule: the skill's "Does its fake retain the information that could be wrong?" is about the fake discarding data; the HEAD fake keeps the packed values (`probe.q[i] = static_cast<float>(input[i])`, HEAD line 261) and the group size (`probe.pack_group_heads = group_heads`, line 259), so the fake retains the information; the gap is in the driver's KV-head count, which predates the PR. "Boundary model shapes" asks for dimensions at supported limits and just outside them; the gated dimensions are head_size and kv_mul (shape_ok / group_heads_ok), and the new 16-head section does drive the supported limit kv_mul 16, while n_kv_heads is not a gated dimension. The PR body does not claim multi-KV-head coverage in this test, so (c) does not apply, but (a) and (b) refute: pre-existing untouched fixture, no real defect, rule not supported. If the author wants the extra coverage it is a follow-up, not a finding on this diff.

The consequence is hypothetical and the gap is not new to this PR. (1) The group base `q.data + kv_head * geometry.kv_mul() * geometry.kv.head_size` [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1696-1697] is unchanged context in the diff (only `<geometry.kv_mul()>` was added on line 1695); it is generic in kv_mul with no group-size literal, so the "4-head era leftover" the finding wants to catch does not exist in the code and cannot be introduced by this diff. (2) `constexpr size_t n_kv_heads = 1;` [t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:82] is unchanged context too (base file line 74): the dispatch test on main already drives kv_mul 4 with one KV head although llama-3.1-8b has 8, so kv_head != 0 was never exercised by this test for any group size. The PR extends the existing fixture to 16 heads and adds per-head offsets to `expected` (lines 142-148) that strengthen the pack check; it does not weaken coverage. (3) The proposed fix is not a drop-in section. With `n_kv_heads = 2` apply_page_range calls pack, QK and PV once per KV head, so `REQUIRE(probe.pack_calls == (packs ? 1 : 0))` [line 199], the qk/pv counts [200-201], `k_tokens_all == calls * n_tokens` [218] and the fake's overwrite of `probe.q` [261] would all need rework, and n_kv_heads would have to become a template parameter; that is a test redesign, not a nit. (4) The PR body already names the end-to-end check of the 2-KV-head model (token identity AMX-on vs AMX-off on Glimmer) as a pending measurement in Open items [pr-body.md:119], and the runtron Glimmer cells ran the 16-head pack at kv_head 1 on all 39 sliding-window layers. A finder-rated "low for a current defect" nit whose fix needs a fixture rewrite is not worth a comment.

judged.title: The "padding stays zero" claim holds only while one group size uses a worker's pack slots; the result does not depend on it, so the comment states a stronger precondition than the kernel needs.
judged.body: Skill rule: trace the changed behavior beyond the diff (consumers of the packed-Q slot) and separate future risks from defects. The comment says the pack slots' padding "stays zero" because the packer "writes only the kv_mul live columns" [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1552-1554]. The slot vector `attn[scratchpad].amx_qpack` is one per worker scratchpad and is shared by every attention operation of the model state [line 1544]. A 16-head pack writes all 16 columns of every panel [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:138-139: `for (size_t q_head = 0; q_head < group_heads; q_head++)`, `dst = packed + ((step * 16 + dim_pair) * 16 + q_head) * 2`]. So in a model whose attention kernels mix kv_mul 16 and kv_mul 4 at head size 128, a later 4-head pack of the same slot would leave columns 4..15 holding the 16-head values, and the stated precondition of pack_q_group_128x4 ("columns group_heads..15 of every panel already zero" [h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp:193]) would be violated. Consequence today: none. Each column of the QK result tile depends on its own packed-Q column only (`_tile_dpbf16ps` accumulates K[token].Q[column]), and the transposing store writes rows 0..group_heads-1 only [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:255-260], so stale padding columns produce discarded values. The PV scratch P is one per instantiation [amx_attn.cpp:284], so it is not shared either. No in-repo plugin has two kernels of different kv_mul at head 128 (llama.hpp declares one kernel [h/tron/plugins/llama.hpp:200-202]; the ingested Glimmer plugin has one geometry per the PR body), so the condition is not reachable now. Evidence strength: high that the condition is unreachable today, high that the result is unaffected if it were reached. Suggested fix (comment only, both sites): say what the kernel actually relies on. For example at line 1552: "resize() zero-fills new slots. The packer writes columns 0..kv_mul-1 of each slot; the QK kernel's result rows depend on those columns only, so whatever the other columns hold does not reach the scores." And drop "already zero" from the pack contract at amx_attn_iface.hpp:193-196, or keep it and add that a model with two group sizes would not satisfy it. Discriminating check: in t_amx_numerics check_qk<GROUP_HEADS_4>, fill columns 4..15 of q_packed with nonzero bf16 values before the kernel call and keep the row 0..3 dotter comparison; it passes today, which shows the precondition is not load-bearing.
judged.rule: Trace consumers beyond the diff; separate design choices and future risks from current defects
judged.evidence:
1552:        // resize() zero-fills new slots and the packer writes only the kv_mul
1553:        // live columns of each slot, so the padding it relies on stays zero
1554:        // (see the pack contract in amx_attn_iface.hpp).
refutations: The finding's own text says the consequence is none and the condition is unreachable; the verification shows it is unreachable by ownership, not only by today's plugin set. The pack slots live in `std::vector<attn_accum> attn;` [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:453], a member of `self_attention<model>::state` [line 236], and one `self_attention<model>` instance has one `geometry`, so one kv_mul: `constexpr bool amx_eligible = amx_attn_h128g4::eligible<...>(geometry.kv.head_size, geometry.kv_mul());` [lines 1537-1539]. Two kernels with different kv_mul would be two self_attention instances with two separate `attn` vectors, so a 4-head pack can never land on a slot that a 16-head pack wrote. The comment at lines 1552-1554 ("resize() zero-fills new slots and the packer writes only the kv_mul live columns ... so the padding it relies on stays zero") is therefore true as written, and the contract at amx_attn_iface.hpp:192-196 already handles the 16-head case explicitly ("For 16 heads every column is written, so that precondition is empty"). That the QK kernel would also tolerate nonzero padding (each `_tile_dpbf16ps` column depends on its own packed column, and `store_transposed_rows<1..3>` run only for GROUP_HEADS_16 [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:255-260]) makes the zero-padding contract conservative, which is a legitimate design choice, not a defect. The proposed fix would weaken a contract that a test checks (`REQUIRE(got == 0);  // padding columns stay untouched` [t/t_amx_numerics.cpp:150]) and would move kernel-internal reasoning into the shared file self_attention.hpp, for no behavioral gain. Not worth a reviewer comment.

judged.title: The P-scratch comment presents zero padding rows and the per-instantiation thread_local as load-bearing for the 4-head result, but the result does not depend on either.
judged.body: Rule: "Review the changed behavior" (identify what the result actually depends on) and "Separate design choices and future risks from current defects"; the same reasoning as the confirmed finding on self_attention.hpp:1552, applied to the second padded buffer this diff touches. HEAD says at amx_attn.cpp:277-283: "rows group_heads..15 are zero padding (never written after thread init), so the padded tile rows contribute nothing. A function template's static locals exist once per specialization. This scratch therefore belongs to the 4-head or the 16-head instantiation only, and a 4-head call never sees a 16-head call's rows." A tile multiply (TDPBF16PS) computes output row i from row i of the A operand only, which Note [Tile stores write 16 rows] itself states [amx_attn_iface.hpp:104-105]. So rows 4..15 of P feed rows 4..15 of `o` only, and callers read rows 0..group_heads-1 [self_attention.hpp:1794-1800]. If a 4-head call did see a 16-head call's P rows, rows 0..3 of `o` would be unchanged. The comment and the PR body ("Is the kv_mul-4 path unchanged? ... The thread_local P scratch is one per instantiation") therefore state a precondition the kernel does not need, and a reader may conclude that sharing one scratch across instantiations would be a bug. Consequence: reading cost and a false invariant that future edits will try to preserve. Proposed replacement for lines 277-283: "rows group_heads..15 are never written by the loop below and stay zero from thread init. They feed only rows group_heads..15 of `o`, which callers ignore (output row i of a tile multiply comes from row i of the A operand; Note [Tile stores write 16 rows]). The scratch is a function-template static, so each instantiation has its own copy." Discriminating check: none needed at runtime; the claim is a property of the tile multiply.
judged.rule: Review the changed behavior: trace what the result depends on; separate design choices from defects
judged.evidence:
amx_attn.cpp:277  // writes raw 16-bit lanes, so this scratch stays uint16_t); rows
amx_attn.cpp:278  // group_heads..15 are zero padding (never written after thread init), so
amx_attn.cpp:279  // the padded tile rows contribute nothing. A function template's static
amx_attn.cpp:280  // locals exist once per specialization. This scratch therefore belongs to
amx_attn.cpp:281  // the 4-head or the 16-head instantiation only, and a 4-head call never
amx_attn.cpp:282  // sees a 16-head call's rows. For 16 heads every row is written, so there
amx_attn.cpp:283  // is no padding.
refutations: Scope (a): the half of the comment the finding objects to most ("rows ... are zero padding (never written after thread init), so the padded tile rows contribute nothing") is pre-existing text. BASE amx_attn.cpp:228-231 already says "rows 4..15 are zero padding (never written after thread init), so the padded tile rows contribute nothing"; the diff only generalizes 4 to group_heads and adds the per-specialization sentences (HEAD 279-283). The finding does not mark that half as pre-existing. The new sentences are factually correct and answer a question the diff itself creates: the loop at HEAD 285 (`for q < group_heads`) writes rows 4..15 in the 16-head instantiation, so "never written after thread init" would be false for a shared scratch. The comment states why the padding rows stay zero; it does not claim that rows 0..group_heads-1 of `o` depend on them. The zero rows are also a documented property, not a false invariant: amx_attn_iface.hpp:103-104 says "Rows group_heads..15 of `o` are the products of the kernel's zero padding rows of P"; a shared scratch would make that sentence false (stale 16-head rows would land in `o`). Rule (b): the tron-code-review text at SKILL.md:21-24 ("First identify the intended behavior... Trace relevant unchanged callers, callees... consumers") and SKILL.md:73 ("Separate design choices and future risks from current defects. Verify that the suspected condition is reachable before calling it a current failure") concern behavior defects. The finding names no behavior defect, no comment-vs-code contradiction, and its proposed replacement keeps every fact of the HEAD text (per-specialization static, rows never written, rows ignored); it only reorders the framing. That is a wording preference, which the task instructions exclude ("style preferences that no rule you were given supports"). The information the finding wants added (output row i comes from A row i; callers ignore rows group_heads..15) is already supplied by the Note the comment cites one line above: HEAD amx_attn.cpp:276 "o holds 16 rows x 128 floats; see Note [Tile stores write 16 rows]", and the Note states exactly that at amx_attn_iface.hpp:103-106. Consumers confirm the comment is consistent with the code: self_attention.hpp:1788-1795 reads rows 0..operation_kv_mul-1 of amx_o only; t_amx_numerics.cpp:273-274 reads rows 0..group_heads-1 only. (c): the PR body (pr-body.md:41) lists the per-instantiation scratch as evidence for the kv_mul-4 path being unchanged, which is true in the object-compare sense the body uses (pr-body.md:63: PV differs only in the thread-local access model); it does not claim the consumed rows depend on it.

The comment at amx_attn.cpp:277-283 states only true facts, and none of them is presented as something rows 0..group_heads-1 of `o` depend on. Its chain is: rows group_heads..15 of P are "never written after thread init" (true: the convert loop at 285-292 runs q < group_heads), and the sentence about per-specialization statics (279-282) justifies that "never written" claim, which would be false under one scratch shared with the 16-head instantiation (whose loop writes all 16 rows). That is a justification of a stated invariant, not a claim that the 4-head result rests on it. The fact the finder wants added, that output row i of a tile multiply comes from row i of the A operand and callers ignore rows group_heads..15, is already in Note [Tile stores write 16 rows] at amx_attn_iface.hpp:103-105, and line 276 of the same comment block points the reader to that Note one line earlier ("o holds 16 rows x 128 floats; see Note [Tile stores write 16 rows]"). So a reader has the dependence picture without the proposed rewording. The per-instantiation sentence also carries real weight for the PR body's "Is the kv_mul-4 path unchanged?" claim: at BASE (amx_attn.cpp:229-231 at 6198824246) rows 4..15 of P were zero and rows 4..15 of `o` therefore zero; with a shared scratch those `o` rows would hold stale 16-head products instead, an observable (if ignored, self_attention.hpp:1792-1796; t_amx_numerics.cpp:274 reads only qi < group_heads) difference from BASE. The "false invariant" consequence is hypothetical: the invariant (padding rows stay zero) is true and costs nothing to preserve. The proposed replacement is a harmless comment-only rewording that would compile and pass tests, but it adds no information the referenced Note lacks, so it does not meet the bar for a reviewer comment even at nit severity.

judged.title: The transposing store selects lanes by `group_heads == GROUP_HEADS_16` rather than by group_heads / ROWS_PER_LANE_4, so a third admitted size would silently store rows 0..3 only.
judged.body: Rule: "Separate design choices and future risks from current defects." This is a future risk, not a current defect: the requires clause at line 192 admits 4 and 16 only, so both branches are correct today. HEAD line 256 reads `if constexpr (group_heads == GROUP_HEADS_16)` and emits lanes 1..3 under it. If group_heads_ok ever admits 8 (the llama-70b / qwen-3-32b family the test at t_amx_numerics.cpp:118-121 names), the 8-head instantiation compiles, passes the requires clause, and writes rows 0..3 of `s` only, leaving rows 4..7 unwritten with no diagnostic. The check_qk sentinel would catch it only if the test were also extended to 8. The PR body defers the general "future shape" question to issue #5021, which is why this is fwiw. A one-line form that derives the lane count from the size keeps the two current instantiations identical: `constexpr size_t LANES = group_heads / ROWS_PER_LANE_4;` then `if constexpr (LANES > 1) store_transposed_rows<1>(...); if constexpr (LANES > 2) ...; if constexpr (LANES > 3) ...;` (4 gives LANES 1, 16 gives LANES 4, 8 would give LANES 2).
judged.rule: Report findings: separate design choices and future risks from current defects
corrections: If posted anyway, drop "silently": admitting kv_mul 8 also requires editing the explicit instantiations at amx_attn.cpp:333-350 (a caller otherwise fails to link) and the static test at t_amx_numerics.cpp:118-121, which asserts kv_mul 8 is refused; and note that the PR body already defers the future-shape requirement to issue #5021.
refutations: Lens (a): the code is new in this diff. BASE amx_attn.cpp has no template, no store_transposed_rows and no GROUP_HEADS_16 (grep of BASE shows GROUP_HEADS_4 only at lines 34, 135, 233), so HEAD line 256 `if constexpr (group_heads == GROUP_HEADS_16) {` is introduced by the PR. That lens alone would keep it. Lens (c) refutes it: the PR body's Open items, "Names" paragraph, says "The rename, together with the requirement that a future shape is a minimal code change, is tracked in issue #5021" (pr-body.md line 123). The finding's whole substance is that a third group size would need a code change at line 256 and would otherwise misbehave, which is the "future shape is a minimal code change" requirement the body explicitly defers to #5021. The finder concedes this itself ("The PR body defers the general 'future shape' question to issue #5021, which is why this is fwiw"). The task instructions exclude anything already answered in the PR body and anything tracked by #5021. Lens (b) also does not support it: the cited rule "Separate design choices and future risks from current defects" (tron-code-review SKILL.md, Report findings section) is a classification instruction for findings that exist; it does not make a self-declared non-defect reportable. The rule's neighbouring sentence, "Verify that the suspected condition is reachable before calling it a current failure", and the HEAD gate at amx_attn_iface.hpp:152-153 (`return g == GROUP_HEADS_4 || g == GROUP_HEADS_16;`) plus the requires clauses at amx_attn.cpp:192 and 265 confirm the condition is unreachable today. The "silently" claim is also overstated: admitting 8 requires editing the explicit instantiation list at amx_attn.cpp:333-350 (otherwise the caller fails to link, as the PR body states) and the static test at t_amx_numerics.cpp:118-121, which asserts `STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE(eligible<tron::bf16>(HEAD_SIZE_128, KV_MUL_8))`, so a widening does not pass unnoticed. Line 256 is the right anchor, but the finding is out of scope.

The consequence is hypothetical and the PR body already answers it. At HEAD the `if constexpr (group_heads == GROUP_HEADS_16)` at amx_attn.cpp:256 is correct for both admitted sizes (requires clause at amx_attn.cpp:192, group_heads_ok at amx_attn_iface.hpp:152-153 admits 4 and 16 only). Reaching the "rows 4..7 unwritten" outcome needs a future edit of group_heads_ok plus new explicit instantiations at amx_attn.cpp:333-354, whose header comment (amx_attn.cpp:330-332) ties the list to group_heads_ok, so the person adding 8 is pointed at this file. The behaviour is also documented right above the branch: amx_attn.cpp:251-254 says the store helper emits lanes 1..3 "only when group_heads is 16". The test already has the sentinel that would catch an 8-head extension: t_amx_numerics.cpp:210 checks rows group_heads..15 of s_amx, and check_qk is called per size explicitly (t_amx_numerics.cpp:321, 324), so adding check_qk<8> is the natural step when a size is added and it would fail. PR body line 123 states the PR is a minimum change on purpose and that "the requirement that a future shape is a minimal code change" is tracked in issue #5021; the task says not to report what the PR body answers, and the finder's own body concedes it is "a future risk, not a current defect". The proposed fix (LANES = group_heads / ROWS_PER_LANE_4 with three if constexpr) would compile and keep the two instantiations' code identical, but it generalises beyond the stated minimum change and would also require rewriting the comment at amx_attn.cpp:251-254; that generalisation belongs in #5021, not in this PR. Not worth a comment even at fwiw.

composed.review_body:
tron-code-review: Short version. This reviewer checked the six touched files at HEAD 5061623a34 for execution-path coverage, shape-gate semantics, packed-Q slot ownership across the two instantiated group sizes (GROUP_HEADS_4 and GROUP_HEADS_16, where kv_mul = query heads per KV head), and whether the new tests can fail when the gate changes. Two findings survived verification: one [nit] on a missing just-outside-the-limit gate row, and one [fwiw] on a comment that states a stronger precondition than the kernel needs. Verdict for this reviewer: approve with nits.

All findings are inline comments.
